title: Tool library file: .camtools drops the drawn cutter (ToolCutter) on export and import
body:
**What happens**

A tool can have a drawn cutter outline (`ToolCutter`, #93 slice 2). The project file (`.camproj`) keeps it in `ToolDto::cutter`. The tool library file (`.camtools`) does not keep it:

- `export_tool_library` (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs`, lines 94-129) writes the tool, its `body` or `holder`, and no `cutter`.
- `parse_tool_library` (lines 137-191) does not read a `cutter` key. `LibraryTool` has no cutter field.
- `ImportTools` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_import/mod.rs`) sets the tool and its body only.

Thus an export and an import give a tool without its drawn cutter.

**Expected**

- Export writes the drawn cutter of each tool that has one, as `[z, r, arc]` points (the `.camproj` form).
- Import reads it and judges it against the tool numbers (`tool_body_wire::cutter_from_dto`, the same check as the project loader). A cutter that disagrees refuses the whole file by tool name.
- `ImportTools` Add, Update and Replace set the cutter, and undo restores the previous cutter, in one undo step.
- A file with a cutter says a new version (5). An older build then refuses the file by version. It does not drop the cutter silently.
- A file without a cutter keeps version 4 or lower, so older builds still read it.

**Why it matters**

- Since #852 the stack laws read the drawn neck of a cutter. A tool that loses its cutter in a library round trip is a different tool for those laws.
- The form mill kind (#3369, plan step D2) keeps its outline in this field. Without this fix, a form mill exported to a library loses its shape.
- This is a leftover of #93 (see the research comment on #93, item 4).

**Done means:** a tool with a drawn cutter makes the same tool after export and import; a cutter that disagrees refuses the file by name; Update replaces the cutter in one undo step; a library without a cutter keeps version 4 or lower. Pinned by tests in `crates/app/tests/tool_library.rs`.

Part of #3663 (plan step D3a). Refs #93.

The filer (qsmits) cannot set labels. A collaborator: please set a priority and an effort label, and `source:agent`. The parent #3663 is `P4`. This changes a file format, thus `effort:high` by the AGENTS.md effort table.

title: Tools: flat-bottom drill kind (180-degree point) - a drill whose tip angle is 180 is refused today

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
**What happens.** CamCraft's tool rules refuse a tip angle of 180 degrees or more (`crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs`: "tip angle ... must be under 180"). A flat-bottom drill (point angle 180, used for flat-bottomed blind holes, drilling on curved or angled faces, and half-hole/intersecting holes) therefore has no place in a tool library: it cannot be created, and an imported library entry for one is refused.

**Evidence of demand.** A third-party converter (Dutchman 0.3.1-rc.7, a library-to-`.camtools` test) drops 48 tools of a real vendor library for this rule alone. Only the count is used here; no library content.

**Expected (general machining practice):**
- A flat-bottom drill is a drill with a 180-degree point: its tip is a flat disc of the full diameter. Drill cycles (G81/G83 and the like) post it like any drill.
- Stock simulation removes a flat-bottomed cylinder; a blind hole's floor is flat, with no cone.
- Hole depth means the flat floor (no tip allowance).
- Verify sees the flat floor (no cone below the programmed depth).

**Done means:** a drill with a 180-degree point is accepted and round-trips through `.camtools`; drilling a blind hole with it simulates a flat floor and posts the depth without tip allowance, each pinned by a test. Other tip angles still keep their current range. Related: #897, #3573 (other hole-making kinds).

title: 2D Contour: with control or wear compensation, check that Plunge and Arc entries cannot reach the wall before G41/G42 engages

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## Problem

PR #3890 (#3888) refuses a Ramp or Helix entry or level transition under control or wear compensation, because those moves reach the wall before G41/G42 engages. The same PR notes an open gap: the Plunge and Arc entries also move under G40 before compensation engages. Nobody tested them against a register larger than the nominal radius, or a positive wear value.

If one of those moves can reach the finished wall before compensation is active, the program cuts the wall silently. That is the same class of defect as #3888.

## Check and fix

- For control and wear compensation, find each move between the end of the rapid and the first move with G41/G42 active, for each entry type (Plunge, Arc, Ramp, Helix) and each side (wall side, bore side).
- Prove from the posted G-code that each such move stays at least the maximum allowed register difference away from the finished wall. Or move the compensation engage before it, or refuse the combination by name.
- Pins on the posted G-code, with an oversized register and a positive wear value: the finished wall is not touched before G41/G42 is active.

## Notes

- Follow-up from PR #3890 (#3888) and the post-merge safety read of #3833.

title: 2D Contour wall-side ramp runs on the ring before G41/G42 engages, so control and wear compensation do not apply to it

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found in the post-merge safety review of PR #3833 (merged 2026-11-24, Fixes #3829).

## What happens

An outside 2D Contour with entry Ramp or Helix now ramps onto each level by a zig-zag along the lead-in and the ring.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_wall_ramp.rs` lines 45-47: the zig-zag path is `flatten(s.e2, &[lead, walk].concat())`. When the ramp run is longer than the lead-in, the legs go onto the ring, next to the finished wall.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_step.rs` lines 127-134: `engage_level` posts these moves before the lead-in.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs` lines 336-348: the compensation span starts at `walk_at - 1`, the lead-in move. `contour_comp::push_span` (`contour_comp.rs` lines 172-178) engages G41/G42 on that move.

The ramp moves are thus posted with G40 active, at the cutter centre that the generator calculated from the nominal tool diameter. `contour_comp::door` (`contour_comp.rs` lines 59-93) does not refuse a ramp or helix entry under control or wear compensation.

Example: a Linear lead-in of 5 mm, a 1 mm level step and a 3 deg ramp angle give a run of about 19 mm. One out-and-back leg is about 9.5 mm, so about 4.5 mm of each leg is on the ring.

## Why it is unsafe

Under control compensation the register holds the real tool radius. Under wear compensation it holds the wear delta. The operator sets these values to put the wall where the program says. The ramp moves on the ring do not get the register value:

- Control: if the real radius is larger than the nominal radius, the ramp cuts the wall by the difference.
- Wear: a positive wear value has the same result.

The finishing pass under G41/G42 cannot restore the cut material. The verifier and the simulation read the nominal centre moves, so the overcut passes silently. Before PR #3833, the wall side had only a graze dive at the lead-in start, which is away from the wall.

## Expected

Do one of these:

- Keep the wall-side ramp on the lead-in only when compensation is in the control. If the lead-in is too short, graze and say why.
- Or refuse a ramp or helix entry on the wall side under control or wear compensation, by name, in `contour_comp::door`.

The bore side (`contour_bore.rs` lines 124-133, `zig_onto` along the same path) has the same pattern. Check it in the same fix.

## Done means

- No feed move of a compensated outside contour runs on the ring outside the G41/G42 span, or the generator refuses the combination by name.
- A test in `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs` sets `Compensation::Control` and `Compensation::Wear` with entry Ramp and Helix on an outside contour. It fails on the current main.

Refs #3833, #3829.

## Problem

PR #3857 (merged) changed `reentry.rs`. It now uses the full-disc test also for tools that do not cut at their centre. Where the old core-only law let such a tool plunge, the operation can now be refused. No pin covers that case. This contradicts the PR's statement that the core law stays unchanged.

Found by a second review of #3857, which the merge overtook.

## Fix

- Decide if the full-disc test is right for tools that do not cut at their centre, and record it in `docs/decisions/`.
- Pin the case: a tool that does not cut at its centre at a 3D Pocket re-entry. Assert the refusal with its name, or the old plunge if the old law was right.

- **With Plunge:** the tool plunges 9 times into uncut stock, with no note and no warning. The advice depends on `AirRoom`, and that case has no air room.
- The stand-in notes (`descent_dive.rs:272` and `:284`, `air_entry.rs:241-247`) are notes only. `entry_status_lines` drops them, and no Warning is posted. So the user sees nothing.
- Pins 2 and 3 of #3748 are green on `main` with this behaviour, so they do not pin it.

## Why P1

A plunge into uncut stock with no warning is an unsafe result that passes silently (Prime Directive). The maintainer ordered that each outcome issue of the #3741 family is P1.

## Fix

- Remove the automatic dead-end ramp for a selected Arc on a plain Outside pocket. If no air entry is possible, refuse the entry with a named diagnostic, or use a safe entry and name it in a **Warning**, not a note.
- A selected Plunge into uncut stock gives exactly one Warning that names the plunge, on the operation and in the status line.
- `entry_status_lines` shows each stand-in entry.
- Pins, red on `main` `1fe369fab` first: a plain Outside pocket with no stock (1) with Arc has no automatic ramp, or names it as a Warning; (2) with Plunge has a Warning for each plunge into stock.

## Notes

- Related: #3748 (closed by #3872), #3567, #3746, #3843.

body:
## Problem

The GPU parity tests (`crates/gpu/tests/cut_onto.rs`, `cut_parity.rs` and others) skip by name when there is no adapter. The gate runs them without `--nocapture`, so the SKIP line is hidden. - Decide, and record in `docs/decisions/`, if the post-merge runner sets `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU` (it has a GPU) or stays at "skip, but report".

## Notes

- Follow-up from the review of PR #3878.

title: UI link on Windows: the CLI does not check that the window on a stale port is the real window

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found in a security review of PR #3861 (part 1 of #3751).

**What happens**

On Windows the link is TCP on 127.0.0.1 with a port that the OS selects (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:221-226`). The discovery file `<pid>.json` holds the port and the token (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:44-57`). A window that crashes does not remove its file (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:159-168` runs only on a normal drop). Only a new window with the same pid replaces it.

The CLI connects to each candidate file (`crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:165-174`):

- `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:101-137`: `open` sends the token, then accepts any peer that answers `HELLO_OK`. The window does not prove that it knows the token.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:133-135`: after the hello, there is no read deadline.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:207-210` and `:249`: `read_line` and `io::copy` read the answer with no size limit.

A different local user can bind the stale port on 127.0.0.1. That user then gets the stale token and the arguments of each tool call (for example file paths). That user can also send false tool results to the CLI, or a line with no end that makes the CLI use all memory. That user cannot run commands in a real window.

On Unix this risk does not occur: the folder is mode 0700 (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:196-204`).

**Expected**

The CLI talks only to the real window. Possible fixes:

- The window proves that it knows the token (for example an answer that includes a hash of the token and a client nonce).
- Before it connects, the CLI checks that the pid in the file is alive, and it removes a stale file.
- The CLI reads each answer line with a size limit.
- Alternative: a named pipe with a user-only ACL replaces the TCP port (the decision in `docs/decisions/3751-cli-ui-link.md` names this option).

**Done means**

- The CLI refuses a peer that does not prove the token.
- The CLI reads answers with a size limit.
- A test in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` starts a false server on a stale entry and shows that the CLI sends no tool call to it.

Refs #3751, PR #3861.

title: UI link: a client without the token can hold the only link session for 5 minutes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found in a security review of PR #3861 (part 1 of #3751).

**What happens**

The UI link serves one client at a time. The token check is on the first line, but the same deadlines apply before and after the token check:

- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:181`: the link uses `IDLE_TIMEOUT` (5 minutes) for its listener.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:233-255`: `accept_loop` serves clients one after the other.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:283-351`: before the hello line, the read loop accepts up to `MAX_LINE` (16 MiB, line 56) and waits up to the idle window.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:330-334`: the token check occurs only when a complete line arrives.

On Windows the link is TCP on 127.0.0.1 (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:221-226`). Each local user can connect to that port. A client without the token can connect and send no newline. It then holds the only session for 5 minutes. It can connect again after the drop. During that time, `camcraft-cli --ui` cannot reach the window. The app also buffers up to 16 MiB for an unauthenticated client.

No command runs, and the UI thread does not stop. This is a denial of service of the link only.

**Expected**

A client that does not send a valid hello line in a short time (for example 5 s) is closed. The hello line has a small size limit (for example 4 KiB). The 5-minute idle window and the 16 MiB limit apply only after the token check.

**Done means**

- A pre-hello deadline and a pre-hello size limit exist in `listen.rs`.
- A test in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` connects, sends no hello, and shows that a second client with the token gets a session after the short deadline.

Refs #3751, PR #3861.

labels.name: source:agent

labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Follow-up of #3843 / PR #3858, from the Opus safety review on PR #3858 (head `215d44a52`).

The law of #3843 (a 2D Offset whose "Pass starts at" is Inside or Outside takes the Arc entry unless the user selects another type) reads only the values before and after an edit; it does not see what the request named. Two doors miss it:

1. **The create door does not get the law.** `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:308-311`: `add_operation` patches the seed and calls `CreateOperation` directly. Probe: `add_operation {"kind":"2D Offset","params":{"pass_start":"outside"}}` gives `pass_start: outside`, `entry: helix` - the bug of #3843 at another door.
2. **An explicit Helix in the same request is replaced with Arc.** `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:323-324`: `edit_operation` merges the patch onto the current params, so the law cannot see a named entry. Probe on a new 2D Offset: `edit_operation {"params":{"pass_start":"inside","entry":"helix"}}` gives `entry: arc` - the user's named choice is overridden. A GUI page that sends the start side and the entry in one edit would have the same problem (only the MCP door was probed).

One rule closes the class: the door tells the law whether the request named an entry, and the create door applies the same law against the seed.

Done means: both probes above give the expected entry (Arc for 1, Helix for 2), each pinned by an MCP test in `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start/start_side_entry.rs`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/3843-start-side-arc.md` lists the named-entry case.

title: 2D Offset one ring set: full-width cuts where the rings of two lobes merge (fig8 waist), and the narrow note does not name them

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
## Problem

The 2D Offset rings merge at concave places where two lobes join. At such merges, corner movements by more than one stepover cause some cuts to take the full tool width without a name.

Readings on `testdata/models/fig8.step`:

| Pass starts at | full-width cut points (`flanks::full_width_points`) |
|---|---|
| Outside (one ring set, #3744) | 495, all at the waist band, Y 40 to 70 |
| Inside (the same ring set) | 10686 (most are first ring along part wall, which is named) |
| Outside before #3744 (rings parallel to stock box) | 0 |

The full-width cuts at the waist are not named. `level_order::full_width_at` measures distance to nearest cut (1.9 tool radii). The ring arms near merge are inside that distance, so "narrow" note does not come. This is a load issue, not a gouge.

## Why P1

AGENTS.md, Prime Directive: a result that is not safe must be refused or the toolpath must give a visible diagnostic. Unnamed full-width cuts can cause cutter overload without warning.

## Fix

- Ring merges should not take full tool width, or they are named on the path.
- Option 1: Use `full_width_at` metric (like flanks meter) to detect ring merge points where steps exceed one stepover distance and emit a "full-width" note.
- Option 2: Apply Held's rule for offset curve merges - smaller local step between ring corners more than one stepover apart.

## Pins

- `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width`: #3744 moved its reading from 0 to "at most 520 points, all in waist band". The fix sets it back to 0.
- A motion pin on a synthetic two-lobe part that reads full-width points at the merge, for Inside and Outside.

Done means: the two pins are green, and no unnamed full-width cut is left at a ring merge.

## Notes

- Related: #3743, #3744.
- This issue was found during fixing of #3744 (one ring set for Auto, Inside and Outside).

title: 2D Adaptive Trochoidal: the clean-up passes are not checked against the engagement limit

labels.name: P3

body:
## Problem

The Trochoidal method of 2D Adaptive checks the tool engagement for each lane. It does not check the clean-up passes after the lanes. A worker that studied #1587 read engagements of up to 102.5 deg on the clean-up passes, against the limit of 90 deg.

AGENTS.md, Prime Directive: a result that is not safe must be refused, or the toolpath must give a visible diagnostic. An engagement above the limit that passes without a note can break the cutter.

## Fix

- Apply the same engagement check to the clean-up passes as to the lanes.
- A clean-up pass above the limit is cut in smaller steps, or it gets a named warning on the operation and in the status line. It never passes silently.
- Pin: on the fixture of #1587, no clean-up move is above the limit without a named warning. The pin is red first on main.

## Notes

- Found during the read-only study for the recommended option on #1587.
- Related: #1587, #3754, #3759.

AGENTS.md, Prime Directive: a result that is not safe must be refused, or the toolpath must give a visible diagnostic. An engagement above the limit that passes without a note can break the cutter.

## Fix

- Apply the same engagement check to the clean-up passes as to the lanes.
- A clean-up pass above the limit is cut in smaller steps, or it gets a named warning on the operation and in the status line. It never passes silently.
- Pin: on the fixture of #1587, no clean-up move is above the limit without a named warning. The pin is red first on `main`.

## Notes

- Found during the read-only study for the recommended option on #1587.
- Related: #1587, #3754, #3759.

title: XYUV wire EDM: auto-detect cap and wall faces from a solid and derive 4-axis sync points

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Detect the two cap faces of a ruled solid automatically and derive 4-axis wire sync points from the connecting wall edges.

## Context

Today `crates/app/src/operation/wire_ruled.rs` requires two picked flat profiles on the top and bottom planes, plus manual `WirePairing::SyncPoints` for twisted parts.
Two outlines alone do not distinguish a cylinder from a hyperboloid, or a spur gear from a skew gear.
Alex's 2026-11-21 design note on `#2690` observes that the two uncut cap faces on a wire-cuttable solid have the highest edge adjacency and near-opposite normals, and that the remaining faces form the ruled walls.

## What this does

- Add a cap-face detector over `FeatureGraph` (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs`) that finds the two planar faces with the highest loop-edge adjacency and near-opposite normals (`dot <= -0.999`).
- Refuse ambiguous solids (for example zero or more than two matching cap pairs, or non-parallel caps) by name instead of guessing.
- Trace wall crease and boundary edges connecting vertices of the upper cap loop to vertices of the lower cap loop to build ordered `WireSync` pairs (`crates/app/src/operation/wire_ruled.rs`).
- Keep manual face, edge-chain, and sync-point selection as an explicit override.
- Route the extracted profiles and derived sync points through `wire_contour_ruled` so the shipped `#2693` and `#2694` swallowtail healers apply unchanged.

## Done means:

- A twisted ruled solid (such as a skew gear or twisted prism) auto-detects its upper and lower cap profiles and derives ordered `WireSync` anchors without manual sync input.
- The generated 4-axis wire path passes `folds`, `crossing`, `lean_law`, `clearance`, and `sim::verify::wire`.
- Ambiguous solids and non-ruled walls refuse by name, and manual profile and sync overrides keep working.

Part of #2690

**What's missing.** The browser build (#1103, #31) is served at `https://neotech.github.io/Camcraft/app/`. `release.yml` builds it, and a failed wasm build only leaves the "not part of this copy" page plus a warning. Nothing checks afterwards that the published page loads and starts: a page that serves HTTP 200 but whose module fails to instantiate, or a site-only redeploy (#3276/#3313) that drops the `wasm-app` artifact, would go unseen. - the page and its module, wasm and shim files load (no 404s);
- the shell reaches its ready state within a time limit, with no console error;
- the version it reports matches the newest published tag (or the site branch's).
A failure becomes an issue (`P3`: the published app does not start; a workaround is the desktop build).

title: Release smoke test: install and run every published release file after a cut (incl. the Intel half of the macOS universal build)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
**What's missing.** Tests cover each platform's *code* (post-merge gate on Linux, the release gate at a cut, Windows quick checks on two Windows boxes), but nothing checks the *packages* `release.yml` publishes. The 0.26.0 release has 11 files: Linux `.tar.gz`, AppImage, `.deb`, `.rpm`, flatpak, snap, Arch `.pkg.tar.zst`, macOS universal `.dmg`/`.zip`, Windows `setup.exe`/`.zip`. Of these, only the macOS zip's contents are listed in the workflow (`unzip -l ... | grep`). None is installed or started. A bad `.deb` dependency, a broken flatpak, a missing asset folder in the `.dmg`, or an installer that does not start would ship unnoticed. The **x86_64 half of the macOS universal build never runs anywhere**.

**Proposal (no Actions minutes; collaborator machines):** after `release.yml` publishes a tag, one script downloads every asset, checks `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and on a box of that platform:
- installs/unpacks it the way a user would (AppImage, `.deb`, `.tar.gz` on Linux; `.rpm` and flatpak on an rpm/flatpak box; `.dmg` on a Mac; `setup.exe` silent install on Windows);
- runs `camcraft-cli --version` (must name the tag) and a small headless job: import the bundled example part, generate, post, and compare the posted program with a committed expected output;
- on a Mac, runs the same job a second time under Rosetta (`arch -x86_64`), which exercises the Intel slice of the universal binary (not Intel GPUs, not speed).
Results: one line per file (PASS/FAIL + reason) as a comment on the release PR / the cut's tracking issue.

**Optional, maintainer's call:** a real Intel check on GitHub's `macos-15-intel` runner (the last x86_64 macOS image, supported until about Aug 2027), one short job per cut (about 50 billed minutes at the macOS rate).

**Done means:** after a cut, every published release file has a PASS/FAIL line from an install-and-run check, including the x86_64 macOS slice under Rosetta; a failing file is named before users hit it.

Related: the browser build at `/app/` (separate issue), the release-tier cut runner (#1413).

body:
Reported timing on a plate with about 8.5k facets and inside rings (entry helix, helix
angle 4, level keep_down):

| rings | time |
|---|---|
| 1 | 4 s |
| 2 | 7.6 s |
| 4 | 20 s |
| 8 | 70 s |

That is about n^1.5. `max_stay_down` does not help.

Finding. All timings are from a debug build (local repro, 43,268 facets, 1/8 in tool, entry helix, helix angle 4,
`level: keep_down`, `transition: ramp`, inside rings picked on the plate):

| rings | moves | kernel `contour()` | `verify_bodies` | `generate` total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 541 | 1.7 s | 29.3 s | 31.1 s |
| 2 | 2,173 | 2.3 s | 115.2 s | 117.7 s |
| 4 | 4,909 | 3.9 s | not isolated | 378 s |
| 8 | 9,865 | 6.1 s | not isolated | 1,018 s |

Without keep_down: 65, 150, 305 and 630 moves; 5.6, 8.9, 21.5 and 54.2 s.

- The kernel is not the cause: 6 s for 8 rings.
- About 94 percent of the time is `verify_bodies` in `generate.rs`. It costs about 54 ms for each
  move with 43k facets, with or without keep_down. The cost is linear in the move count.
- Keep_down posts 8 to 15 times more moves for the same rings (the ramp legs), so it is
  8 to 15 times slower. A slower growth than linear in the rings comes from the larger rings.
- `solid_hits` already has a `SolidIndex`. The slow sub-step inside `verify_bodies` is not isolated.
  It needs a profiler inside `verify_bodies`.

Needed: find the slow step in `verify_bodies` for a long ramped path, or cut the move count of a
keep-down ramp. A STEP model with 4 to 14 mm through holes reproduces it (not attached here).

title: Design: MCP / AI Chat "script mode" on the existing cam JS engine (run / job / look) to cut agent cost and tool calls

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
@NeoTech, a design question for you. The idea and its measurements are @dudedagger42's: his SolidCraft script-mode work, carried over to CamCraft here. (mkinney is following this closely.)

**Prior art.** tangency-labs/solidcraft#12642 by @dudedagger42 added a "script mode" (scx) to SolidCraft's MCP server. The agent got three tools instead of dozens: `run` (a short script in a CAD vocabulary), `design` (state) and `look` (a view). Every `run` reply ended with a diff of what changed. Measured on SolidCraft's benchmarks: **59% less cost per task and 58% fewer tool calls at the same accuracy**, holding on Haiku, Sonnet and Opus. SolidCraft's maintainer closed it **only because it embedded a Python interpreter** ("will never ship a Python interpreter, sandboxed or not"), not because of the idea.

**Why CamCraft is in a better position.** CamCraft already ships a sandboxed JavaScript engine (boa) with the job-script API: the `cam` global, `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts`, VERBS in `crates/app/src/script/mod.rs`. There is no fs, no fetch and no console, and every side effect is a `cam` verb that rides the command history. A script mode would therefore need no new interpreter and no new host access.

**Proposal (to decide, not yet to build):**
- `run`: execute a short `cam` script as **one undo step**. The reply ends with a compact diff: tools and operations added or changed, op statuses, warnings, verify result. It refuses by name on the first failing verb, and rolls back the step.
- `job`: a compact document summary (not the full `get_job` JSON).
- `look`: a text or image view to check the work.
- The usual MCP tools stay for clients that want them. Script mode is an option of `camcraft-cli mcp` and of the in-app AI Chat.

**Why it matters now:**
- The reporter's measured AI Chat session cost about $0.45 per prompt, mostly from re-sent tool lists and large JSON results (#3784).
- Fewer round trips give faster replies.
- One script maps to one "Undo Turn".
- Local models handle 3 tools far better than about 150 (#3789's benchmark: small models fail most change tasks).

**Open questions:**
1. Does the `cam` verb set cover the common chat requests (add tool, add op with params, generate, verify, post, stock and WCS)? Which MCP tools lack a verb?
2. Is a diff reply enough to check the work, or does `look` need a render?
3. Do we keep both modes, and which is the default for AI Chat?
4. Safety: script verbs go through the same commands and refusals as the GUI. Confirm that no verb bypasses a check.

**Done means:** a decision comment here. If yes, a first measured slice: the 20-task local-model benchmark (`~/bench/local-models`) plus one cloud model, run with the current tools vs. script mode, reporting cost, calls and accuracy, followed by sub-issues for the build.

Related: #3784 (chat cost), #3789 (model recommendations), #3783 (providers).

body:
Found during #3746 (PR #3823), after the merge of #3818 (`7f4915a6d`, the in-plane ring links of #3747).

## What happens

Setup: `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start.rs`, `fig8_world()`, 2D Offset, Pass starts at Outside, EM-0800-4FL, the Arc entry (`offset_op_entered(..., PassStart::Outside, Entry3D::Arc)`).

The pass link at the end of a piece at (47.429, -39.000) does not keep down. The tool lifts to clearance and rapids 162 mm across the part to the next pass start at (46.482, 123.140). The same lift occurs at Z 12.000, Z 2.000 and Z 1.500. One more occurs at Z 1.500 to (-46.500, 123.542).

The link notes say:
- `link: the tool lifted to the retract plane 6 time(s) instead of the keep-down level/pass link - the in-plane link would cross a cut planned on that plane; ... (first lift at (47.429, -39.000), Z 12.000)`
- `link: the tool lifted to the retract plane 6 time(s) instead of the keep-down level/pass link - the in-plane link would leave the area that keeps the tool off the part; ... (first lift at (46.488, 123.257), Z 12.000)`

Each next start is in material. The entry code (`entry_restart`) tries, in this order:
1. the air entry of #3746;
2. the ramp along the pass;
3. a clear helix.

None fits, so the start is entered with the named plunge: `entry: the pass start (46.482, 123.140) at Z 12.000 is in material and the arc's lead room is blocked, and no ramp fits clear of prior cuts - plunged into material at the plunge feed`.

## Why the entry code cannot fix it

The start stands inside ring 0, the walk along the stock edge, which is cut first. Each in-plane lead from the air crosses ring 0 at the cut Z, and the verifier's Crossing law holds such a post. The start column has no room for a helix clear of the earlier cuts. The piece is too short for the ramp. Only a link that stays down through cut material (for example along ring 0) reaches the start. That is link or order code (`pass_link`, `ring_links`, `level_order`).

## Done means

- `fig8_outside_offset_has_no_plunge_into_material` (`crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start.rs`) is green. Remove its known-fail marker in the same PR.
- On fig8 Outside, no pass link lifts across the part to a start in material without a named reason that the status line shows.

body:
## Problem

PR #3818 (#3747) applies the ring link law to each `around_part` area that has a chosen pass start. `around_part` is true for each Clearing operation with Outside containment and a stock. This includes a 2D Pocket with Outside containment, as `crates/app/tests/pocket_pass_start.rs` uses it (`pocket_op` sets `Containment::Outside`).

The PR body says "2D Pocket Inside and Outside do not change (#3752)". But the joins and pass links of such a pocket now use the ring law. The review of #3818 found that the change is safe: every link is proved, or else it lifts with a named reason. But no pin covers it.

A second point from the same review: for a ring area, the ring law overrides `Link::Clearance` and `Link::KeepDown`. A failed link lifts to `hop_z` (retract), not to `clearance_z`. A user who selected Clearance can expect the clearance height.

## Fix

Choose one of these, and record the choice in `docs/decisions/`:
1. Narrow the gate to the 2D Offset operation, so that 2D Pocket waits for #3752.
2. Keep the scope, and add pins for a 2D Pocket with Outside containment: no overcut, no crossing, and each lift named.

Also decide if a failed link honours the user's `Link::Clearance` choice. Pin the result.

## Notes

- P1 by the maintainer's rule: each outcome issue of the #3741 family is P1.
- Related: #3752 (2D Pocket on the shared ring set), #3743.

title: Column stock: simulate copies the whole cut history on each call, so a program cut one move at a time is quadratic

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`stock_sim::cut::simulate` (the column engine behind `Stock::simulate`) copies the stock's whole cut history at the start of each call:

```rust
let mut history = dex.history.as_deref().cloned();
```

The history holds every cut so far. It grows with each call. A caller that cuts a program in small steps (one move for each call) thus copies a longer history at each step. The total time is quadratic in the number of moves.

Expected: the time of a program cut one move for each call is near the time of the same program cut in one call.

### Evidence

We run `camcraft-sim` from a fork as the stock engine of a batch verifier. The verifier reads the stock before each cutting move, thus it cuts one move for each call.

- A 3-axis job on a 2541 x 2100 column stock, 137,940 moves: one call takes 2 s. One move for each call ran for more than 1800 s, and we stopped it.
- With the history grown in place (below), one move for each call takes 6 s. The removed volume is the same to the bit as the one-call cut.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make a column stock: `Stock::block(Backend::Column, 0.0, 0.0, 20.0, 20.0, 10.0, 0.1)`.
2. Make 4000 short feed moves across the block.
3. Cut them in one `simulate` call. Then cut them on a second, new block with one `simulate` call for each move.
4. Compare the times. The second cut is much slower, and the gap grows with the number of moves.

### Proposed fix

Take the history out of the stock, grow it in place with `Arc::make_mut` (this copies it only when another stock shares it), and put it back. On a refusal, truncate the cuts to their old count and put the history back, so the stock stays as it was (`add_ops` only appends cuts). We have this change and a pinning test on our fork. We will open a PR from a branch `issue/3819-history-in-place` if you accept the claim.

Not in scope: `carried::clip_columns_under` uses the same copy, but it runs one time for each setup, not for each move.

### Version and OS

v0.26.0 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `P3` (slow with a workaround: cut in one call), `effort:high` (stock simulation is under the safety floor).

Done means: a pinning test in `camcraft-sim` cuts 4000 moves one call at a time on a column stock. Each column top is the same to the bit as the one-call cut, and the time stays inside a linear budget.

title: 2D Adaptive on the stock: a stock margin narrower than the tool is refused as "pocket is narrower than the tool", with no band, width or fix named

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found by the reporter in v0.26.0 via the AI Chat panel (2026-11-23). Reproduced headlessly with the 0.26.0 `camcraft-cli`; the same code is on `main`.

## What happens

A 2D Adaptive on the stock (source `stock`, no boundary picks) around a 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.27 mm plate, stock from **fit stock** (2 mm per side, top Z 3.27), with a 3 mm end mill (catalog `EM-0300-2FL`), on the Tormach 770MX (ML), refuses at generate with:

```
2D Adaptive1: invalid machining parameters: pocket is narrower than the tool
```

The refusal is right (the area to clear is the 2 mm band of stock around the part, and a 3 mm cutter has no legal position in it), but the message does not say that. There is no pocket in this job, so "pocket" points the user at the wrong thing. It does not say which area is narrow, how wide it is, by how much the tool misses, or what to change. The in-app assistant read it as a missing boundary selection or a too-small helix radius (0.6 mm), and neither is the cause.

Readings (box stock, `dz` 5.27, side margin m per side, same tool and op):

| margin per side | result |
|---|---|
| fit stock (2 mm, Z -2..3.27) | refused: "pocket is narrower than the tool" |
| 1 mm | refused, same text |
| 2 mm | refused, same text |
| 3 mm (= tool D) | generates (Offset rings fallback, notes) |
| 4 mm, 6 mm | generates; the #1655 band note and corner note appear |

So the band check that #1655 added (`machining2d::unreached_note` through `operation::keep_law::narrow_noted`) names a narrow band only when some other part of the area produced a path. When the whole area is one band narrower than the tool, the generator refuses first, with the bare sentence, and the band note never runs.

## Steps to reproduce

`simple.step` is a 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.27 mm plate STEP (any plate of that size works). Script `a.js`, run with `camcraft-cli script a.js`:

```js
cam.import("simple.step", "simple");
cam.call("load_machine", {builtin: "Tormach 770MX (ML)"});
cam.call("fit_stock", {});            // 29.4 x 29.4, Z -2..3.27: 2 mm per side
cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0300-2FL"});
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Adaptive", tool: "EM-0300-2FL", source: "stock"});
cam.generate();
```

Output: `generate: 2D Adaptive1 - could not generate the toolpath: 2D Adaptive1: invalid machining parameters: pocket is narrower than the tool`. Replace `fit_stock` by `set_stock {box: {dx: 31.4, dy: 31.4, dz: 5.27}}` (3 mm per side) and it generates.

## Expected

A refusal that says what is narrow and what to do, e.g. "2D Adaptive1: the stock around the part is a band 2.000 mm wide, narrower than the 3.000 mm tool (plus 0.000 mm stock to leave): no cutter position fits. Widen the stock to at least 3.000 mm per side, use a tool under 2.000 mm, or cut the outside with a 2D Contour." The same refusal stays a refusal (no path is emitted); only its words change. Where the area is a real pocket (a part source, a closed boundary), the text names the pocket and its narrowest width the same way.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs` `pocket_started_on` (the site this job hits: `non_sliver_center(region, off)` empty -> `GenError::Invalid("pocket is narrower than the tool")`), and the same bare sentence in `adaptive_avoid.rs`, `pocket_avoid.rs`, `rest2d.rs`, `rest_prior.rs`, `corner_relief_spur.rs`, `adaptive/rest/mod.rs`.
- `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs` `narrow_noted` / `machining2d::unreached_note` (#1655): already measures the band; it could word the refusal when the whole stock-around-part area is one band.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs` `name_outside_entry_refusal` already adds advice to this sentence, but only for Outside containment (#2232), not for the stock source.

Related: #1655 and #1554 (the band note on a generated path), #3631 (warn at edit time when the tool cannot fit a pocket; this issue is the generate-time refusal text, not the edit-time warning).

Priority P3 ("a misleading message" with a workaround: widen the stock or pick a smaller tool). Effort medium: the refusal stays a refusal and no toolpath, gouge check or posted G-code changes (so the safety floor does not apply); the work is wording in the 2D pocket family plus reuse of the existing band measure, with a test.

Done means: on the reproduction above (stock-source 2D Adaptive, 2 mm stock margin, 3 mm tool) generate is still refused, and the refusal names the stock band around the part, its width (2.000 mm) against the tool (3.000 mm), and at least one fix (wider stock or smaller tool), without the word "pocket"; a pinning test in `crates/app/tests/` asserts that text, and the existing "narrower than the tool" asserts still pass.

title: 2D Offset one ring set: full-width cuts where the rings of two lobes merge (fig8 waist), and the narrow note does not name them

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Found while fixing #3744 (one ring set for Auto, Inside and Outside). Related: #3743.

## What happens

The one ring set of #3744 is the offsets of the part. At a concave place of the part, the offsets of two lobes merge. At the merge, the corner of each ring moves by more than one stepover from the corner of the next ring. Thus some cuts there take the full tool width.

Readings on `testdata/models/fig8.step` (the `offset_pass_start` heavy fixture: EM-0800-4FL, stock margin 5 mm, Outside containment):

| Pass starts at | full-width cut points (`flanks::full_width_points`) |
|---|---|
| Outside (one ring set, #3744) | 495, all at the waist band, Y 40 to 70 |
| Inside (the same ring set) | 10686 (most are the first ring along the part wall, which is named) |
| Outside before #3744 (rings parallel to the stock box) | 0 |

- The full-width cuts at the waist are not named. `level_order::full_width_at` measures the distance to the nearest cut (1.9 tool radii). The ring arms near the merge are inside that distance, so the "narrow" note does not come.
- This is a load issue, not a gouge. The gouge and crossing checks are clean on this pass.

## Expected

- The rings at a merge do not take the full tool width. One option: clean-up rings or a smaller local step between two ring corners that are more than one stepover apart (Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", 1991, covers the merge of offset curves).
- A cut that still takes the full width is named on the path, by the same law that the flanks meter uses.

## Pins

- `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (heavy): #3744 moved its reading from 0 to the bound "at most 520 points, all in the waist band". The fix sets it back to 0.
- A motion pin on a synthetic two-lobe part that reads the full-width points at the merge, for Inside and Outside.

Done means: the two pins are green, and no unnamed full-width cut is left at a ring merge.

## Request

The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-23. His words: "Aur package; should rebuild the Linux build that comes before it and not rebuild it again from scratch.. Waste of time and action credits." He set the priority P2.

## Problem

In `release.yml`, the AUR package step compiles CamCraft again from the source. The `linux` job of the same run has already built the same release binaries from the same tag. The second build costs time and billed GitHub Actions minutes (AGENTS.md: the minutes are budgeted).

## Expected

- The AUR package uses the Linux release binaries that the `linux` job of the same run made. Use an artifact (`actions/upload-artifact` in the `linux` job, `actions/download-artifact` in the AUR step), or the release asset of the same tag.

- The PKGBUILD that we publish stays correct for AUR users. If the AUR rules need a from-source PKGBUILD, publish it unchanged, and only the CI check of the package uses the prebuilt binaries. Record which way was chosen, and why, in `docs/decisions/`.
- The packaged binary is byte-identical to the binary in the Linux release asset. A check compares the checksums.

## Notes

- This changes a file in `.github/workflows/`. Use the `runners` skill. Add no trigger. The maintainer ordered this change.
- Measure the minutes of a tag run before and after, and put the numbers in the PR body.
- Test the change with a `workflow_dispatch` dry run, not with a new tag.

## Work

1. Bring our solidcore fork up to date with its upstream. Use a merge, never a force-push. Record the upstream commit that the fork now contains.
2. Change the git reference of solidcore in the workspace `Cargo.toml` to the new fork commit. Pin a full commit `rev`, not a branch.
3. Update `Cargo.lock` for solidcore and its new transitive dependencies only.
4. List each new or changed transitive dependency and its license in the PR body. A new dependency needs the maintainer's decision (`needs-maintainer`).
5. Keep the third-party notices in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` current.

## Why effort:high

Solidcore meshes the STEP models (#916, #917). A new mesh can move toolpath pins, as #2849 shows. This is under the safety floor: geometry and toolpaths.

## Checks

title: Circular: cut the rings of a level in one walk at depth; no lift and no new entry into material at each ring

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Part of #3743. Builds on step 1 (#3750). Step 5 of the migration.

## The maintainer's words

#3741: "Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

#3741 rule: "Each ring goes around the part in the plane of the cut and stays at depth. The tool does not lift between the parts of one ring."

## What happens

Circular has its own ring code: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs:233-340` (`rho = rc - stepover * k` at `:289`, the Inside order at `:288`, the rim helix at `:300`). It walks each ring as its own ladder (`run_level_walks` for each ring, `:340`). Each call makes a new `WalkState` with `first: true` (`levels.rs:328-329`). Thus each ring enters again from the clearance height, and each entry goes down into material. The rings are not linked at depth.

## Fix approach

1. Circular gets its rings from `ring_set` with the circle input. The rings stay exact G2/G3 circles at the same radii.
2. One walk for each level over all rings. The link from ring k to ring k+1 is a stepover link at depth by `ring_links` (a radial line or a tangent arc in the cut plane).
3. One entry for each level by `ring_entry`. The rim helix stays as the entry where the tool must enter material.
4. A lift needs a named reason.

## Pins

- `circular_rings_link_at_depth`: a circular pocket with 4 rings has one entry and 0 lifts on each level.
- `circular_rings_unchanged`: the ring radii and the arc count of each ring are the same as on the head before this change.
- Equivalence: the verifier verdicts and the gouge checks of `crates/motion/tests/circular_arcs.rs`, `crates/motion/tests/circular_ring_links.rs` and `crates/app/tests/circular_ring_links.rs` do not change, except the lift and entry counts.

Effort `max`: a new link law for Circular, under the safety floor. Priority P1: a needless lift and an entry into material at each ring.

Done means: Circular rings come from `ring_set`, each level has one entry, and the pins are green.

title: camcraft-cli: a --ui flag sends commands to the running UI, and --skill installs an AI skill for the CLI

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
## Request

The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-23. His words: "Make the camcraft-cli able to interact witht he ui. By adding the flag --ui, so it instead sends it commands directly to the UI and changes gets reflected in the UI. This allows for alot better interaction and end2end testing, for dealing with UI improvements and for endusers also doing setups. The CLI improvements should come with a --skill <folder,claude,copiplot> install creating a AI skill for working with the CLI tool."

The maintainer set the priority P2.

## Part 1: `camcraft-cli --ui`

- With `--ui`, the CLI does not run the commands in its own headless world. It sends them to a running CamCraft UI.
- The UI runs each command through the same undoable command history as the GUI ("Everything Is a Command"). The change shows in the UI at once, and Ctrl+Z undoes it.
- The CLI prints the result of each command and returns a non-zero exit code on an error, as in headless mode.
- When no UI is running, the CLI gives a clear error. It does not fall back to headless mode silently.
- Uses: end-to-end tests of UI changes, agent-driven checks of the UI, and set-up of a project by a user from a script.

Questions to decide (record each in `docs/decisions/`):
1. The transport: a local socket or a named pipe. Find the UI with a discovery file in the user's data folder. Bind only to the local machine.
2. Security: accept only local connections from the same user. Use a token in the discovery file. Never listen on a network port.
3. The protocol: reuse the MCP tool surface (`crates/app/src/mcp/`) so that the CLI, MCP and the GUI call the same commands. Do not make a second command set.
4. Several UI windows: select one by project path or process id.
5. Windows, Linux and macOS from the same source ("Stays buildable everywhere").

## Part 2: `camcraft-cli --skill <target> install`

- `<target>` is one of `folder`, `claude` or `copilot`.
- `folder`: write the skill files into a given folder.
- `claude`: install the skill where Claude Code reads skills, for the user or for the project.
- `copilot`: install it where GitHub Copilot reads custom instructions.
- The skill text comes from one source in the repository, and it lists the CLI verbs, the `--ui` mode and examples. Relate it to #1947 (single-source AI agent skills) and to the existing `camcraft-mcp` skill.
- A test checks that the installed skill names each CLI verb that exists (a drift test).

## Pins

- A UI test starts the app through the test harness, sends one command with `--ui`, and checks that the UI state changed and that undo restores it.
- A CLI test with no running UI checks the clear error and the exit code.
- A test for each `--skill` target writes into a temporary folder and checks the files.

## Notes

- This is new design (an IPC transport and a protocol), thus effort:max.
- Slices are permitted: part 1 first, then part 2.

body:
Part of #3741. Builds on #3746 (the air entry) and #3747 (the in-plane links).

## The maintainer's words

"you would never helix on a outside cut.. as you dont need to "lead in" like that.. so an outside cut would default to a ARC or straight approach in the plane of its cut, starting outside the stock boundary with a given value."

From the #3741 comment: "An Outside cut never uses a helix entry, and it does not use a ramp entry." Pin: "an Outside pass has no helix move and no ramp move into material, and that each entry starts outside the stock boundary."

## What happens

A start-side pass can still enter by a helix or a ramp at four places:

1. The first entry of a level: `descent.rs:216-286` (`plan_arm`) with the user's Helix or Ramp; `descent.rs:131-136` (a helix stands down to a ramp).
2. The #3577 dead-end ramp: `level_ramp_entry.rs:100-127` (`dead_end_ramp`), marks at `level_order.rs:143-145`, plan check at `level_rings.rs:108`, call at `ladder_links.rs:188-191`. Decision: `docs/decisions/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end.md`.
3. The #2265 solid restart between passes: `ladder_links.rs:200-211`.
4. The centre-cutting law stand-ins: `descent.rs:137-148`.

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part; see the #3741 research comment): Outside on `main` has 366 ramp moves (13 dead-end ramps). On `47aa341ff^1` the same 13 re-entries were plunges or helices.

## Fix approach

1. After #3746 and #3747 a start-side pass has one entry for each level (the air entry) and no re-entry into uncut stock. The dead ends of #3567 do not exist with the contour-parallel rings of #3744.
2. Remove `dead_end_ramp`, its marks (`ramp_starts`) and its plan check. Update `docs/decisions/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end.md` with a "superseded by #3741" line.
3. On a start-side pass, a restart that would need a helix or a ramp lifts and uses the air entry, or the op is refused with a named reason. It never helixes or ramps into stock.
4. Rewrite the pins of `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement.rs` that assert a ramp ran. The late-entry pin counts every entry into stock again (no ramp exemption).

## Pins (red first)

- `start_side_pass_has_no_helix_or_ramp`: Inside and Outside on the dog-bone part and on `testdata/models/fig8.step` have no helix move and no ramp move below the material top.
- `start_side_entries_start_outside_the_box`: each entry of a start-side pass starts outside the stock box by at least the tool radius plus the approach distance.
- `outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock` (existing, `pass_start_engagement.rs:181`) stays green with no ramp exemption.

Effort `high`: removal of one entry law and its pins, under the safety floor.

Done means: the pins are green, `dead_end_ramp` is gone, and the #3567 decision file names #3741.

title: 2D Offset Pass starts at Inside and Outside: enter in air outside the stock box, then an arc lead-in in the cut plane with Arc radius and Arc sweep

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Part of #3741. Builds on #3744 (one ring set) and #3745 (the approach distance).

## The maintainer's words

"The arc atm, is showing as a "straight" plunge down.. which is fine for transporting to the plane, but it should happen outside the stock box. - and also we see no movement of a an arc to wal into the wall of the stockbox - so no viable approach is getting generated using the Arc approach. The Arc Sweep and Arc Radius inpputs does nothing to affect the approach"

About Inside: "picking "inside" makes perfect rings, but the cutter planges straight down into the material.. instead of starting outside the stock box"

## What happens

Inside and Outside share one entry path: `ladder_links.rs:55-92` (`descend`) -> `descent.rs:120-149` (`plan`) -> `descent.rs:216-286` (`plan_arm`). One fix covers the two.

1. The entry is placed at the first point of the first pass (`descent.rs:217`). For Outside that point is on the stock edge. For Inside it is at the part wall, in solid stock.
2. The `Arc` entry is a vertical-plane arc onto the first cut (`entry.rs:37-41`, `descent.rs:262-277`). Its lead chord is proved against the cutter-centre area (`descent.rs:271`). For Outside that area ends at the stock box, so the air outside the box is never legal. `entry_arc.rs:146-152` returns "the arc's lead room is blocked".
3. `descent_dive.rs:169-187` (`substituted_dive`) then posts "axial dive on the floor instead". Its fix text (helix radius, start hole) does not apply to a start side.
4. The horizontal (G17) arc entry (`arc_xy`, `descent_xy.rs:205-220`) is skipped when the arm is `Arc` (`:218-219`), and it proves only inside the legal area.

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part, 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2; see the #3741 research comment):

- Outside, Arc entry: the first dive has its tool centre 0.50 mm INSIDE the stock box. Arc radius 4 -> 10 and Arc sweep 90 -> 45 do not change the path.
- Inside, Plunge entry: 8 plunges; the first one is 8.41 mm inside the box, in solid stock.
- Same on `e313aa663` (#3353): this is not a regression of #3577.

## Fix approach

A new entry law for a start-side pass (Inside and Outside, and Auto through #3744):

1. Rapid to a point P outside the stock box. The distance from P to the box is at least the tool radius plus the approach distance (#3745).
2. Feed down in air at P to the cut Z.
3. Feed in the cut plane: an optional straight lead, then a G17 arc of Arc radius and Arc sweep, tangent onto the first ring. Arc radius and Arc sweep come from `Approach::arc_radius` / `arc_sweep`.
4. Prove the lead path against the stock box grown by the approach distance and the tool radius, not against the cutter-centre area. It must not touch the part or a fixture. Where no lead fits, refuse with a named reason. Do not post a silent plunge.
5. Outside: the first ring is at the stock edge, so the lead runs in air and enters the stock wall on the arc.
6. Inside: the first ring is at the part wall, and stock can enclose it. Recommended option (the maintainer's words): the entry still starts in air outside the box, and the in-plane lead feeds through the stock to the first ring. This feed is a slot at the full tool width, so it uses the plunge feed and the status line names it. Dropped: a helix in material for Inside (the maintainer asks for an air entry). Record the choice in `docs/decisions/`.
7. Check the Lead in / Lead out page. The maintainer saw Helix, Ramp and Plunge disabled for Outside. That page code was not found on `main` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/lead_page.rs:25-44, 89-102` show all four kinds). Make the page offer only Arc and a straight approach for Inside and Outside.

## Pins (red first, from the maintainer's comment)

- `outside_entry_plunges_in_air`: the plunge XY is outside the stock box by at least the tool radius plus the approach distance.
- `outside_first_cut_is_an_arc_in_the_plane`: the first cutting move after the plunge is a G17 arc at the cut Z.
- `arc_radius_changes_the_lead`: a change of Arc radius changes that arc's radius in the output; a change of Arc sweep changes its sweep.
- `inside_entry_is_no_plunge_into_material`: no entry of an Inside pass is a straight plunge into material (the maintainer's pin).
- `start_side_entries_have_no_helix_or_ramp`: no Inside or Outside entry is a helix or a ramp.

Effort `max`: a new entry geometry with a new legal-area proof, under the safety floor.

Done means: the five pins are green on the dog-bone part and on the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step`.

title: Post scripts other than Haas write a whole-number F word without a decimal point

labels.name: bug

body:
**What happens**

#3681 fixed the Haas post: each F word now has a decimal point (`F600.`). The scripts below still write a whole-number feed with no point (`F600`). This table comes from a read of origin/main 6866890b6.

| Post | F formatter (lines) | Whole-number F has a point? |
|---|---|---|
| carvera.cps | `ff` 84, `fw` 87 | no |
| doosan-dnm.cps | `ff` 193-196, `fw` 200, `feedWord` 1047 | no |
| fanuc.cps | `ff` 155-158, `fw` 162, `feedWord` 968 | no |
| fanuc-lathe.cps | G98: `capWord` 688 -> `fm` 683; G99: `feedWord` 313-318 -> `fr` 270 (`pt`) | G98 no; G99 yes |
| grbl.cps | `ff` 87-90, `fw` 93 | no |
| grblhal.cps | `ff` 93-96, `fw` 99 | no |
| heidenhain-klartext.cps | `rate` 61-68, used at 277, 306 | no for a whole value |
| heidenhain.cps | `ff` 70, `fw` 84 | no |
| linuxcnc.cps | `ff` 141-144, `fw` 147 | no |
| mach3.cps | `ff` 92-95, `fw` 98 | no |
| mach4.cps | `ff` 103 (`trimDec(..., keepDot=false)`) | no |
| mazak.cps | `ff` 128-131, `fw` 135 | no |
| sinumerik.cps | `ff` 83-86, `fw` 89 | no |
| tinyg.cps | `ff` 93-96, `fw` 99-107 | no |
| tormach-lathe.cps | `feedWord` 227-230 -> `fr` 186-189 | no |
| tormach-plasma.cps | `ff` 60, `feedWord` 300-306 | no |
| tormach.cps | `ff` 109-112, `fw` 115; A-axis `floorWord` 890-893 | no |

These scripts are correct already or have no F word: sinker-iso.cps (keeps a point), agie-native.cps (stub), sodick-wire.cps and wire-iso.cps (no F word found).

**Why it can be wrong**

On a Haas control, Setting 77 scales an integer F word (#3681). No public manual of the other controls was checked for the same rule. Some controls read an integer F as a whole feed, so the output can be correct there. A control with a setting like Haas Setting 77 reads the feed wrong.

**What should happen**

For each post, find the public programming manual of the control:
- If the manual says that the control scales an F word with no point, add the point. Make that control a `P1` defect, in its own issue or here.
- If the control cannot read a point in an F word (for example Klartext or a GRBL dialect), keep the present form and record the source.

**Done means**

- Each row has a cited manual section, and the post writes the F form that the manual specifies.
- Each changed post has a test that fails on an F word in the wrong form.

Found during #3681 (PR #3689).

title: Verifier: a feed plunge deeper than one stepdown into material that the levels above did not cut passes with a centre-cutting tool

body:
Found while working #3453 (issue-worker-high). The coordinator set P1: the verifier passes an unsafe entry silently.

## What happens

A 2D Contour with tabs posts a feed plunge of 18 mm into sheet that no level above cut (#3453, #3678). `verify` gives `ok: true` with no findings.

Evidence:

- The reporter of #3453 ran `verify` on CamCraft v0.25.0 (q07, MDF bracket, 18 mm sheet). The result was `ok: true`, no findings, for a plunge from Z2 to Z-18 with a 2.8 mm crescent of uncut sheet beside the cutter.
- After the #3453 PR, the motion fixture `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs` shows two tab window dives with the full tool disc in uncut stock: Z12 -> Z-18 at (-5.165, -4.266) and (-4.796, 44.676), stepdown 4.5 (#3678 has the tables).
- Code read (context pack of #3453, origin/main 44c13a01d, not changed since v0.25.0):
  - `crates/motion/src/plunge_law.rs:91`: `guard` returns at once for a centre-cutting tool. A centre-cutting tool is the default (`approach.rs:256`, `tool_table.rs:138`).
  - For a tool that is not centre-cutting, the law reads the axis core only (`plunge_law.rs:56`, reach `tool_r * (1 - CORE)`), not the full disc.
  - `crates/sim/src/verify/`: no law compares a feed plunge depth with the stepdown, or with the floor that the cuts before it left under the disc. `rapids.rs` law (d) judges lateral rapids. `contact.rs:117-119` treats a plunge as the entry from air.
  - The wall-side entry notes are advisory (`contour_step.rs:120-127`).

Not verified here: a fresh `verify` run on the current main for the #3453 fixture. The worker ran motion tests only.

## Expected

`verify` names a feed plunge that goes deeper than one stepdown (or a stated limit) below the stock that the earlier cuts left under the full tool disc. The finding blocks the post, or it is a named warning that the user must see. A silent `ok: true` is not permitted.

Done means: a verify test with a recorded program that has such a plunge gives a named finding, and the #3453 catalog case gives the same finding until #3678 is fixed.

title: 2D Contour: a tab window dive plunges deeper than one stepdown into material that the levels above did not cut

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while working #3453 (issue-worker-high). This is part (2) of that issue. The coordinator split it out of the #3453 PR.

## What happens

A tabbed level of a 2D Contour enters each tab window at the start of the window's lead-in. The levels above cut that lead-in only at the ring start. At every other window, the lead-in start lies in material that no level above cut. The dive feeds from the retract plane to the tabbed level in one plunge move.

Fixture: `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs` (L-shape 40 x 40 with a 25 x 25 notch, Outside, `bottom_z` -18.3, stepdown 4.5, 4 tabs 10 x 3, tool D6, Plunge entry, Arc lead r3, clearance 25, retract 12). "Floor" is the lowest level pass whose swept disc holds the point. "Disc floor" is the highest floor under the full tool disc.

Before #3453 (origin/main 44c13a01d), PLANAR links:

| level | window | entry XY | plunge Z | floor under centre | disc floor | below disc floor | crescent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -18 | 0 | (46.000, 8.865) | 2 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 1 | (10.153, -6.000) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 2 | (-6.000, 29.525) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 3 | (21.000, 30.029) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |

After the #3453 PR (window 0 enters at the untabbed start; the tab layout ends the tabs on the spacing marks from the start), PLANAR links:

| level | window | entry XY | plunge Z | floor under centre | disc floor | below disc floor | crescent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -18 | 0 | (43.514, -5.802) | 2 -> -18 | -15.3 | -15.3 | 2.7 | 0 |
| -18 | 1 | (-5.165, -4.266) | 12 -> -18 | 0 | 0 | 18.0 | full disc |
| -18 | 2 | (-4.796, 44.676) | 12 -> -18 | 0 | 0 | 18.0 | full disc |
| -18 | 3 | (18.186, 19.500) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | -15.3 | 2.7 | 0 |

With the stay-down ramp preset (`level: KeepDown`, `transition: Ramp`), the untabbed levels below the first do not cut the lead-in. After #3453, window 0 of the -18 level plunges 2 -> -18 at (43.514, -5.802) with the disc floor at -4.5: 13.5 mm below the floor.

With Lead None, each window dive is on the ring, in the kerf of the level above: 2.7 mm below the floor. That case is correct.

## Expected

No feed plunge of a contour goes deeper than one stepdown below the floor that the levels above left under the full tool disc at that XY.

## Proposed fix (from #3453)

- A guard on the wall-side graze dive (`contour_step.rs` `graze`) and the tab-window dive (`contour.rs`, window `k > 0`), for each level below the first level of its ring.
- Read the floor under the full disc from the moves that the builder has posted (flat feed passes and plunge columns).
- If the dive goes deeper than one stepdown below that floor, peck: plunge one stepdown, rapid up, plunge the next step. Say it in one note.
- The uncut floor is `min(entry top, first ring level + stepdown)`, so a first level and the shelf bands do not change.
- An alternative is to cut the window lead-ins on the levels above. Compare the two.

Done means: `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs` asserts that every descent of the three presets is at most one stepdown below the disc floor, and the pinned window 1 and 2 readings change to that.

body:
Found in the review read of PR #3668 (the catalog case `3d/rough-finish`, #2866). Read from the posted program; no machine run. Refs #2392.

**What the program does:** between two levels the tool makes a rapid straight down to the Z of the floor that it cut in the level before, with no margin. Examples: line 63 `G00 X-23.98 Y-24.03 Z20.`, line 1625 `G00 ... Z10.`. The lowest Z on a rapid line of the program is Z10.

**Risk:** a rapid that ends in contact with a floor that was cut a moment ago. A small error of the tool length, or chips on the floor, makes it a rapid into material. The usual practice is to stop the rapid a feed distance above the floor and to feed the rest.

**Expected:** the rapid stops at the feed height above the last cut floor (the feed height of the operation), and the rest is a feed move.

**Done when:** a test on this case finds no rapid whose end is nearer to cut or uncut material than the feed height. The catalog program is then made again.

body:
Found in the review read of PR #3668 (the catalog case `3d/rough-finish`, #2866). Read from the posted program; no machine run. Refs #2392.

**What the program does:** the entry of the operation is a helix, and each level starts with a helix. But in a level the tool goes in again about 29 times with a straight feed plunge from the clearance height. Each of these goes into a row where only about half of the tool width is cleared, and the full stepdown of 2 mm is stock.

**Example** (lines 126-128): `G00 X8.081 Y-9.48 Z47.` / `G00 X-8.072 Y-9.48 Z47.` / `G01 X-8.072 Y-9.48 Z16. F300`. The row at Y-12.48 cleared up to Y-9.48; the band from Y-9.48 to Y-6.48 has stock from Z18 to Z16. The same at line 1634 (`G01 X-7.199 Y-21.48 Z8. F300`).

**Expected:** a re-entry uses the entry type of the operation (a helix or a ramp), or it goes down only where the full tool disc is in cleared stock. A tool that does not cut at its centre must not get a straight plunge into stock; check that the centre-cut law judges these moves.

**Also:** each entry feeds the full 39 mm from Z47 at the plunge feed, and the roughing has 16 moves of zero length.

**Done when:** a test on this case finds no feed move that goes down into uncut stock outside a helix or a ramp. The catalog program is then made again.
