body:
Found in the review read of PR #3668 (the catalog case `3d/rough-finish`, #2866). Read from the posted program and the model; no machine run. Refs #2392.

**Case:** a 50 x 50 x 8 mm plate with a spherical dome (apex at Z18), box stock to Z22, 3D Pocket with a 6 mm flat end mill, stepdown 2 mm, stock to leave 0.5 mm.

**What the program does:**
- The level at Z18 is a full raster over the apex of the dome, which is at Z18. Line 83 (`G01 X24.48 Y-0.48 Z18.`) passes 0.0006 mm from the apex. The allowance there is 0, not 0.5 mm.
- The last level is Z8, the top of the plate. The allowance on the floor is 0.
- On the flanks the measured allowance is 0.21 mm to 0.38 mm (at Z16 the edge of the tool is 0.21 mm from the sphere), not 0.5 mm.

**Expected:** the roughing leaves the stated allowance in each direction, or the operation has two values (wall and floor) and says which one it applies.

**Risk:** the part is not cut below its surface. The finishing pass gets less material than the user stated, and on the floor and the apex it gets none.

**Done when:** a test measures the smallest distance from the roughing path (tool envelope) to the model on this case, and it is not below the stated allowance less the tolerance. The catalog program `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.nc` is then made again.

title: UI proposal: a Tool library dialog with first-class holders, a large tool drawing and recipes

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
## Summary

This issue proposes a new design for the tool library. It is a proposal for discussion. It contains no code.

The "Tool library" tab on the right side becomes one dialog. The **Tools** cell of the ribbon opens it. The dialog has two kinds of item: tools and holders. Each kind has a list, a rail and an editor with a large drawing.

### Pictures

**1. Tool list** (Document, My library, Catalog; categories on the left)
![Tool list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/1-tool-list.png)

**2. Tool editor** (the list is a rail; parameters, the assembly group and the drawing)
![Tool editor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/2-tool-editor.png)

**3. Recipes tab**
![Recipes tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/3-recipes.png)

**4. Holder list**
![Holder list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/4-holder-list.png)

**5. Holder editor**
![Holder editor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/5-holder-editor.png)

Interactive mock-up (one HTML file, no network access; download it and open it in a browser): https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/blob/1acd3beb0b0e9378b06074e3e2615ba7cd5d89f4/tool-library-proposal/mockup.html

## What we have today

- "Tool library" is a tab beside Properties (`tool_library::draw`). It lists the built-in catalog with an "Add" button.
- A tool is edited on a property page with four folded groups: Geometry, Holder, Cutting data and Catalog (`tool_settings_grid::grid`).
- The holder is a combo box inside the tool (`tool_holder_picker`). The holder library is built in (`holder_library.rs`).
- The tool drawing is a 260 px square (`tool_preview::draw`).
- The cutting data of a tool is a table of `CuttingRow` entries, one for each work material.

## The proposal

### 1. One dialog, opened from the ribbon

- The **Tools** cell of the ribbon opens the dialog. The tab on the right side goes away.
- The header has a switch: **Tools | Holders**.
- The first screen is a list. Categories are on the left. Items are on the right.
- A click on an item opens its editor. The list folds into a narrow rail on the left. The user can go from item to item in the rail. An arrow goes back to the full list.

### 2. Tools

- The list has three sources: Document, My library and Catalog.
- Each row shows: a small drawing, the T number, the name, the type, the diameter, the flute length, the number of flutes, the holder, the gauge length and the number of recipes.
- The editor has three tabs: **Tool**, **Recipes** and **Details**.
- The parameters are on the left. The drawing is on the right.

### 3. Holders are first-class items

- Holders have their own list. The list is grouped by spindle taper.
- Each row shows: the name, the taper, the clamp, the clamping range, the gauge length, the largest diameter and the number of tools that use the holder.
- A holder has its own editor: the machine side (taper), the tool side (clamp and clamping range) and the shape.
- The holder editor lists the tools that use the holder. A change to the holder updates each of these tools in one undo step.
- The list shows which taper the mounted machine takes. The holder picker of a tool marks the holders with a different taper.

### 4. One home for each field

Today some values are in two places. The proposal gives each value one owner:

| Owner | Fields |
|---|---|
| Tool | Cutter (diameter, flute length, corner radius, angles, flutes, helix, tool material) and shank diameter |
| Holder | Taper, clamp, clamping range, gauge length of the holder, largest diameter, shape |
| Assembly (tool in holder) | The holder that the tool uses, and the stick-out |

- The assembly is one boxed group at the bottom of the Tool tab.
- The gauge length of the assembly is not typed. The dialog shows it: holder gauge length + stick-out.
- The same group shows if the shank diameter is in the clamping range of the holder.
- A link in the group opens the holder in its editor.

### 5. A large drawing

- The drawing is to scale, from the tool tip to the spindle nose.
- It shows the cutter, the shank and the holder.
- It shows dimension lines: diameter, flute length, stick-out, gauge length and shank diameter.
- It shows the flutes as helix lines, from `flutes` and `helix_deg`. This is decoration only. It adds no geometry law.
- The user can switch off the dimensions, the holder and the flutes.
- The drawing changes when the user changes a value.

### 6. Recipes

- The **Recipes** tab shows one row for each work material: spindle speed, feed, stepdown and stepover.
- Below each row the dialog shows the surface speed and the feed per tooth.
- A mark shows the row of the work material of the document. Operations use that row.
- Buttons: "Add material", "Suggest feeds and speeds" and "Copy recipes from tool".
- The data is the `CuttingRow` table of today. Plasma and waterjet tools keep their own recipe columns.

## What does not change

- Each Apply is one undoable command: `AddTool`, `ChangeTool`, `SetToolBody`, `ApplyCuttingData`. The MCP tools stay as they are.
- The file formats (`.camtools`, PathPilot `.csv`, Hurco `.TCM`) stay as they are.
- The page tests `layout_page_tool` and `layout_page_tool_library` need a new home as `layout_window_*` tests.

## Relation to open issues

- #3645 (user library store): "My library" needs it. This dialog is its front end.
- #3648 (component library browser) and #808 (holder library follow-ups): the Holders list and editor.
- #2452 and #3642 to #3647 (component-based tool assemblies, ISO 13399): a tool, a holder and a stick-out are the smallest assembly. The assembly group can grow into the assembly editor (extensions, inserts).
- #3393 (cut recipes GUI): the Recipes tab.
- #93 (spun design editor): "Edit outline" in the holder editor can open it.

## Open questions

1. Dialog or dockable window: can the user keep it open beside the viewport?
2. User-made holders need a store and a file format. Is that part of #3645?
3. Is a recipe one row for each material on the tool, as today? Or is it a shared object with a name (#3393)?
4. Does this dialog become the assembly editor of #2452?
5. Which part is the first slice? Suggestion: the dialog with the Tools list and the editor, on the data model of today. Holders and "My library" follow when their stores exist.

## Notes

- The mock-up uses the default dark theme tokens and the tool fields of `main`.
- No material of another CAM product was used.
- The pictures are mock-ups made in HTML. They are not pictures of the application.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: A .camtools library cannot hold a form-profile mill, a blunt tapered mill, or a single-form thread mill without a pitch range

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
CamCraft at c5bb09ed13f8b63e691d3a5ed6fb0be6a64ee2aa.

## What other tool libraries store

Fusion tool libraries store three kinds of mill that a `camcraft-tools` definition has no field for:

1. Form mill: a drawn profile, a list of (radius, height) points from the axis at the tip, round the cutter and back to the axis. It covers thread mills, double-angle cutters, radius-profile cutters and any ground shape.
2. Tapered mill: a cone with a tip diameter (flat) or a corner radius (ball) at the tip, a taper angle per side and a shoulder diameter at the cutting length (tapered engravers, ball-tip tapered mills).
3. Single-form thread mill: one tooth in the profile; Fusion states no pitch range (the range is in the description text, if anywhere).

## What is missing

- `kind: taper` is a cone from a sharp apex. A tool with a tip diameter or a ball tip has no field; writing it as `taper` shifts the cone by half the tip diameter at every height.
- The drawn cutter outline (`set_tool_cutter_profile`, `ToolCutter`) exists in a project but a `.camtools` definition cannot carry it (`tool_edit` lists `cutter` as not here), so an arbitrary form profile cannot travel with the tool. `kind: form` is a lathe gauge.
- `thread_mill_single` needs `pitch` and `pitch_min`; a source that stores only the tooth has neither.
- Smaller: the dovetail check `top < sr` compares with no tolerance, so a neck that meets the flank exactly (head 6.096 mm, 1.4605 mm high, 45 degree flank, neck 3.175 mm) is refused by float dust: `3.048 - 1.4605 / tan(45 deg)` is one ulp under `1.5875`.

## Synthetic example

Form mill, mm: profile `(0,0) (2,0) (4,0.8) (2,1.6) (2,9) (4,11) (4,40) (0,40)` (one 43.6 degree V tooth on a 4 mm radius shank).
Tapered mill, mm: tip diameter 1, taper angle 30 degrees per side, cutting length 10, shoulder diameter 12.

## Ask

Any of: a `tip_d` (and ball radius) on `taper`; an optional `cutter` outline in the definition, judged by `cutter_profile::check`; an optional `pitch_min` default for `thread_mill_single`; a small tolerance in the dovetail neck check.

Until then Dutchman writes only the multi-form thread mill (rows of equal teeth at one pitch, read from the profile) and the sharp-tipped taper, and reports the others as not carried over.

## Measured

On a 97-tool Fusion library: 85 written, 12 not written (11 single-tooth form mills, 1 tapered mill with a ball tip). One multi-form thread mill and one dovetail now convert.

## What to build

Add UI browsing for compatible tool components and an Assembly Builder in the Tool Editor (`crates/ui`), following `crates/ui/AGENTS.md` and the `ui -> app -> flecs` layering rule.

1. **Component Library view** in the Tool Library dock (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_library.rs` and new sub-module):
   - Browse built-in, user-library, and document components by kind (`Inserts`, `Holders`, `Adapters & Extensions`, `Parametric Tools`).
   - Add a "Compatible holders" / "Compatible inserts" filter on any selected component using `compatible_parents` and `compatible_children`.
   - Allow saving a component to or deleting a component from the user library.
2. **Assembly Builder** in the Tool Editor (extending `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_body_assembly_page.rs`):
   - Display the tool's linked component stack (mount -> adapter/extension -> holder -> insert) with port names, Z-rotation, and projection controls.
   - Show derived cutting parameters and gauge length as read-only values driven by the assembly.
   - Offer one-click component swap filtered to compatible components, plus "Edit shared component" (showing how many tools use it) and "Detach to standalone tool".
   - Show an update badge and a "Sync from library" button when a document component differs from the user library.
3. Route every document change through the undoable app commands (Everything Is a Command).

## Notes

- Depends on the document commands and persistence sub-issues of #2452.
- Update structural layout tests (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/page_layout.rs` / `structural.rs`), never snapshot PNGs.

## Done means

- Headless UI tests in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/` verify filtering holders that accept a selected insert, assembling a turning tool from linked components, live update propagation across two tools when editing the shared insert, syncing from the user library, and undo/redo.
- Existing UI layout and behaviour tests stay green without lowering the `#[test]` count.

Part of #2452

body:
Wire `.mch` URDF machine models into `camcraft-simview` (`camcraft-sim` checks and playback) and record the #2593 decisions.

## Context
Research in #2593 defined the URDF file contract across `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-geometry`, and `camcraft-sim`. `camcraft-simview` (#2586) owns the mapping from `camcraft_post::machine::MachineTree` into `camcraft_sim::machine_model` so `camcraft-sim` keeps no edge to `camcraft-post`.

## Scope
- In `crates/simview`, when `MachineTree::urdf` is present, resolve `urdf.file` relative to the `.mch` file directory and build the `MachineModel` through `camcraft_sim::machine_model` instead of generating loose blocks (#2584).
- When `MachineTree::urdf` is absent, keep the existing `.mch` model path (#2584, #2591).
- Feed posed URDF bodies into the machine-part collision check and playback renderer. Do not label URDF findings or passes as "judged on a generated model".
- Keep `.mch` `travel` authoritative in `MachineCheck`, print any URDF vs `.mch` limit discrepancy notes, and report a URDF mechanical joint limit overrun as a failed check (exit 2, with NC line number).
- Refuse a missing, unreadable, or invalid URDF or mesh with exit 1 and the named diagnostic; never fall back silently to a generated model.
- Add `docs/decisions/2593-urdf-machine-model.md` recording the research decisions of #2593 (`.mch` key and joint map, SI unit conversion, root frame, `.mch`-wins limit law, STL/OBJ scope, pure-Rust XML reader, and dropped options).

## Done means
Tests in `crates/simview/tests/` pin `camcraft-sim check` on a 3-axis NC program with a `.mch` referencing a URDF + binary STL fixture: a machine-part collision fails with exit 2 without the generated-model tag, a mechanical joint limit overrun fails with exit 2, a missing URDF or mesh refuses with exit 1, and a `.mch` without `urdf` still uses the generated model. `docs/decisions/2593-urdf-machine-model.md` exists.

Depends on #2586, #3638, and #3640.

Part of #2593

labels.name: in-review

labels.name: source:agent

body:
Found in the second safety read of PR #3058 (#1883). Refs #1882, #1885.

**Now (with PR #3058):**
- The operation has no standoff height. The cut plane is the top of the sheet (`crates/app/src/operation/waterjet_op.rs:96`, `cut_z = top`). Plasma has `cut_height`.
- The CL has no jet on/off record and no pierce dwell record. Travel moves are rapids at the clearance plane; lit moves are feeds. The pierce dwell and the abrasive delay are in the path notes only.
- No shipped post serves `Kind::Waterjet`. But a user script can declare `serves = ["waterjet"]` (`posting_serves/tests.rs:9`). That script gets this CL: no jet on/off, no dwell, and the nozzle tip on the sheet for a machine with a Z axis.

**Risk:** a nozzle that touches the sheet, or a jet that is not switched, on a machine that runs a user post. No shipped post can do it.

**Wanted (one of the two, the first is smaller):**
1. The post gate refuses a waterjet operation by name until the jet records (#1882) and the waterjet laws (#1885) are in. The refusal says what is missing.
2. Or: add the standoff height to the operation (validated above the sheet top) and the jet on/off and dwell records to the CL.

**Also:**
- The stock simulation skips Probe, Torch and Wire, but not Waterjet (`stock_sim.rs:288`). The nozzle goes into the dexel simulation as a cutter at the sheet top. `verify` gives no visible "not judged" note for a waterjet operation. A kind that no law judges must say so.
- Corner slow-down, taper and kerf lag are not modelled. Say so in the path notes or in the decision file.
- With a lead-in of 0 the pierce is on the kerf ring at the edge of the part, and no note says so.
- The label "In control (G41/G42)" uses G-code words (the plasma page has the same label). The row label "Tab position" is there two times (`waterjet_page.rs:110`).

title: 2D Pocket: warn at edit time when the tool cannot fit the pocket

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: `set_tool`, `add_operation` and the UI accept a tool that is too wide for a 2D Pocket. The generator refuses it later with "pocket is narrower than the tool". Found during #3475.

Why #3475 did not fix it: the fit of a pocket depends on the region that the generator cuts. That region depends on the containment (an open side lets a wider tool cut from outside), the stock and the part slice (`operation::selection_region`, `pocket_region_memo`, area controls). The command does not have that region without these steps. A bounding-box or width estimate can refuse legal work, so #3475 added none.

Also owed (same rule, other doors):
- `EditOperationParams`: an edit of a plain Slot's `width` or `stock_to_leave` that makes the current tool too wide is not refused at the command. #3475 refuses only at create, at `set_tool` (`EditOperationLinks`) and at a `ChangeTool` that widens the tool. The shared rule is `camcraft_motion::machining2d::slot_centre_band` and the sentence is `operation::tool_gate::slot_fit_refusal`.

Expected: an accepted pocket edit with a named `warning` in the MCP reply (the `clearance_warning` pattern of `edit_operation`), and the same text in the UI, when the generator's own predicate (`non_sliver_center(region, r + stock_to_leave)` is empty) says that the tool cannot fit. The check must use the same region as generate, or it must not run.

Done means: a pinning test shows the warning for a too-wide tool on a closed Inside pocket, and no warning for an Outside pocket that the generator cuts; a Slot width edit below the tool is refused at the command with the #3475 sentence.

title: No way to open a project read-only: Save can write over a reference copy

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
**What happened**

CamCraft cannot open a project read-only. Every open project saves over its own file:

- In the window, Save writes to the file that was opened (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:3436-3440` on `main` 60b19abe8).
- The MCP tool `save_project` without a path, and the script call `cam.save()`, write to the file that was opened (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:41-52`).
- `camcraft-ui` has no read-only option. `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` stops with `unknown option '--read-only'` (`crates/ui/src/cli_options.rs:192`).
- The MCP tool `open_project` takes only `path`. `open_project {"path": "job.camproj", "read_only": true}` is refused with `open_project: unknown argument "read_only"` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs:115-123`).

These users need a project that opens without a risk to its file:

- a user who opens a shipped example or a tester kit to look at it;
- a person who reviews a released job;
- a team that keeps reference copies on a shared folder.

CamCraft already has this behaviour for shipped machines. The machine editor refuses Save for a shipped machine, and Save As writes a copy (`crates/app/src/machine/draft.rs:35-36`, `:229-242`, `:259`).

**Expected**

- `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens the project read-only.
- A save over the opened file is refused on every save route: the window, MCP `save_project` and script `cam.save`. The file stays byte for byte.
- Save As to another file works, and the project is then no longer read-only.
- The title bar says that the project is read-only.
- An agent can open a project read-only with `open_project {"path": ..., "read_only": true}`.

An open SolidCraft pull request adds the same option, `solidcraft --read-only` (tangency-labs/solidcraft#20830). The same name and behaviour in both apps help users who use the two.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Copy a project file, for example a shipped example, to a folder.
2. Run `camcraft-ui --read-only <copy>.camproj`. The start stops with `unknown option '--read-only'`.
3. Run `camcraft-ui <copy>.camproj`. Change a parameter and push Save. CamCraft writes over the copy.
4. In `camcraft-cli mcp`, call `open_project {"path": "<copy>.camproj", "read_only": true}`. The call is refused: `open_project: unknown argument "read_only"`.

I found this by code inspection.

**camcraft version and OS**

`main` at 60b19abe8 (2026-11-22). Windows 11.

**Proposed change**

- A new start option `--read-only` in the option table (`cli_options.rs`). It applies to the one project file on the command line. A model file is imported as usual, because an import makes a new project with no file. A headless start ignores it.
- One rule in `crates/app/src/project/`, `project::refuse_read_only_save`, next to `project::save` and its other refusals. It refuses a save to the file that the project is open read-only from. The window's `save_project_path` and `script::api::v_save` call it. `v_save` serves MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live MCP seam of a window.
- The rule compares files, not spellings (canonical paths), because the Save As dialog gives an absolute path.
- In the window, Save on a read-only project opens the Save As dialog, as the shipped-machine editor does. A save to the opened file from the dialog is refused on the status line.
- Changes stay allowed in memory.
- MCP `open_project` gets an optional `read_only` boolean. Scripts get it through `cam.call("open_project", ...)`. The live seam still refuses `open_project`, but the window's read-only state reaches a live `save_project`.
- The title bar shows `CamCraft - job.camproj (read-only)`.
- No file-format change. `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change.

**Done means:** `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens the project read-only and the title says so. Tests show that a save over the opened file is refused, and that the file stays byte for byte, through the window, MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live seam. Tests show that a save to another file works and ends read-only. A test shows that the option parses and keeps the file argument. The help text, `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`, the site guide and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` describe it.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: Verifier: the tangency law slices the model one time for each distinct Z (34.7 s on a ramp entry)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Found by the work on #3588 (PR for `band_reach`). Refs #3567, #3577.

## What happens
The tangency law (b), `section::tangency` in `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs` (about lines 74-147), takes one island slice for each move. The slice is at `min(from.z, to.z) + lift` (`section.rs:96`), through `Rest::islands_at`. The island cache (`rest.rs:146-157`) keys on the exact bits of Z. A ramp entry has a different Z at each move, so each move pays one full slice of the model.

Measured by the worker of #3567 in debug, on `pocket_pass_start::fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` with PR #3577: tangency takes 34.7 s for 2232 moves that are not planar (about 15 ms for each slice). Planning takes 0.21 s.

#3588 fixes the cost of `band_reach` only. `band_reach` uses the same slices; for a flat cutter (`lift` 0) on a descending ramp they are the same cache keys, so the slice cost is paid one time, in tangency.

## Why this needs its own design
The slice itself is the cost, not the use of it. Each plane gives a different Region: a face of two triangles crosses each plane at a different point. A reuse of one slice for a Z interval, or a snap of the key, changes the section that the law judges. That is a change of a gouge check, under the safety floor.

Possible directions (not decided):
- Slice incrementally: sort the facets by Z span, and keep the active set between two planes.
- Prove that two planes with no facet vertex between them give the same verdict for the law, and reuse the slice for them.
- Measure the release build first: if it is seconds there, lower the priority.

## Done means
- A path with about 2000 distinct cut Z values verifies tangency in a time that does not grow with moves x slice cost, or the release time is measured and found small.
- The findings of the tangency law do not change on the existing tests (an equivalence test against the old law).

body:
Split out of #897 (which also covers spot drill, countersink and center drill, P8): the two hole-making kinds that real tool libraries need most now.

**What happens:** `ToolKind` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs`) has no reamer and no counterbore. Such a tool can only be stored as a `Drill` or `EndMill`, losing what makes it different, or not at all.

**Why now:** converting one user's real tool libraries to `.camtools` (14 libraries, community converter bnegt/Fusitool2Craftool), 2487 reamers and 42 counterbores were skipped because CamCraft has no kind for them - the largest group of unconvertible tools after missing feed/speed data. CamCraft already has the cycle side: reaming (G85) and dwell/boring cycles shipped with #1445.

**What the kinds need (from general machining references - Machinery's Handbook, ISO/DIN reamer and counterbore standards, public tooling catalogs):**
- **Reamer:** diameter, flute length, number of flutes, lead (chamfer) angle and length, overall/shank; its cutting data runs slower than a drill of the same size (per-material rows, #890); a hole op with a reamer uses the reaming cycle and expects a pre-drilled hole (finish allowance).
- **Counterbore:** cutting diameter, pilot diameter (or none) and pilot length, flat bottom, flute length; a hole op cuts to a stated depth with a dwell at the bottom.
- Both: spun outline that the simulation and the reach/gouge checks read (safety floor: effort high), `.camtools` file version bump with old files still loading, MCP `add_tool` / `edit_tool` kinds, catalog entries.

**Clean-room:** specify geometry and behaviour from the public references above. Do not use Fusion's tool-library schema or the converter's Fusion-side code (also GPL-3.0) as a spec - the converter only showed how many tools are missing.

**Done means:** a reamer and a counterbore can be created, saved and reloaded in `.camtools`; a reaming op and a counterbore op generate, simulate and verify clean on a plate fixture with the tool's real outline; old `.camtools` files load unchanged; pinned by tests.

title: Face with 'Do not touch': blocked lower levels leave the face above Cut Z, and only a note says so

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found in the second read of PR #3413 (head b38f0c12f). The label `bug` applies.

## What happens
A Face operation with protected items clips its rows by a keep-out. The keep-out of a level covers the heights from that level up to the clearance plane. A lower level gets the same keep-out or a larger one. Thus the blocked levels are always the lowest levels.

When one or more levels are blocked and one level stays clear, the operation generates. The face can stop above Cut Z in each place. The only sign is the note "blocked N facing level(s); the remaining levels stayed clear" (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/face_keep.rs:425-429`).

The note does not say that Cut Z was not reached. Nothing marks the operation "incomplete". The Prime Directive says: "If an operation can only be computed in part, mark it 'incomplete'."

The result is not a gouge. Material stays that the user expects to be removed.

## Wanted
- When a blocked level leaves the face above Cut Z, the operation says so in plain English with the depth that it reached, and it is marked "incomplete" (or refused: record the decision).
- A test with a keep-out that changes with Z (an item that is wider at a lower level) pins the message and the state.

## What happens

ProfileCutout: 2D Contour, side outside, picked outer chain, entry plunge, stepdown 4.5, 4 tabs (width 10, height 3), bottom = bottom of model - 0.3, Router up-cut 6 mm. The untabbed levels (Z -4.5, -9, -13.5, -15.3) all lead in at the same point (X258.066 Y2.09), so each plunge is one stepdown into the kerf of the level above. The first tabbed level moves the lead-in to the inside corner of the L and plunges from Z2 straight to the final depth:

```
G0 X242.068 Y1.89 Z25
G0 X246.667 Y90.812 Z25
G0 X246.667 Y90.812 Z2
G1 X246.667 Y90.812 Z-18 F600
G1 X253.739 Y87.072 Z-18 F1950
```

The upper levels cut along Y 88 there (kerf Y 85..91), so the Ø6 cutter centred at Y 90.812 (Y 87.8..93.8) plunges 18 mm with a 2.8 mm crescent of never-cut sheet beside it, at the plunge feed. Each tab hop then also feeds from Z -18 up to Z 12 and plunges 30 mm back down at F600 (lines 464-470 and on). The same happens on the Z -18.3 level. `verify` reports `ok: true`, no findings.

## Expected

Each level enters at most one stepdown below the floor the levels above left at the entry point (the same lead-in point as the untabbed levels, or a ramp), and tab hops rise only to the tab top plus a clearance.

## Repro files

[q07-router.camproj](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.camproj), [q07-router.step](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.step), posted [q07-router.nc](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/q07-router.nc) (operation ProfileCutout from line 372; the tabbed level at lines 456-490); agent report [REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q07-router-mdf/REPORT.md) problem 8.

How bad: no gouge of the part; a full-length plunge into partly uncut stock that the program's own stepdown says never happens, a cutter-breakage risk on small router bits.

Done means: on this project every ProfileCutout level enters no deeper than one stepdown below the cut floor at its entry point (pinned by a test with tabs on a multi-level contour), and verify or the op notes name a plunge deeper than the stepdown into uncut stock.

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> issue; enhancement; support for tapered tooling like ball mills, roundover bits and similar, router style tooling.

Part of #3351. Refs #3351. Sub-issue 9 of the plan in #3351.

Depends on #3370
Depends on #3371
Depends on #3372

## What to do

A form bit cuts an edge, not a wall. This is a new law, not an offset by a radius (the #3351 body says the same). It is slice 1, step 3 and step 4 of the research in #896, for a non-undercut `FormMill`.

1. Edge form law in 2D Chamfer: the user gives the edge loop and the form depth. The cutter axis rides at the offset `rho(z_low)` from the wall, where `z_low` is the lowest height of the form band. The tip height puts the top of the form band on the top face. For a roundover of radius `R` and pilot radius `r_p`: offset `r_p`, and the arc meets the wall and the top face tangentially.
2. The pilot band clears the wall by the gouge tolerance. The pilot never touches the part.
3. `EdgeBreak` (`crates/cl/src/cl/edge_break.rs`) and `credit_breaks` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/edge_break.rs`) credit a circular break and a general form break (the meridian swept along the edge), beside the planar bevel of today.
4. Where the model already has the rounded edge, the cut must match it with no credit.
5. Trace and Engrave admit a `FormMill` with a non-decreasing meridian (a groove or bead along a line).
6. Open the 2D Chamfer door that #3369 closed, for a non-undercut `FormMill`.

## Rules

- `effort:max`: a new toolpath law (safety floor).
- The `Taper` chamfer toolpaths and goldens do not change (pinned).

## Done means

- A roundover bit rounds the top edge of a brick in 2D Chamfer, verifies clean, passes `posting::verification_gate` and posts (pinned, with a golden). This is the "Done means" of #896 for corner rounding.
- A cove bit and an ogee bit cut their form along an edge to the given depth with no gouge under `deviate` (pinned).
- A cove groove along a line in Trace simulates to its form (pinned).

This is slice 2 of the research in #895, made general for any meridian, and the column part of #896 Q5.

1. Column engine (`crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` `plan_ops`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/dexel.rs`, `dexel_arc.rs`): one revolved atom set from the meridian, beside `dexel_bull.rs`. Each convex atom cuts with the existing convex search along straight and arc moves.
2. Field engine (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_solid.rs`, `field_cut.rs`, `field_sweep.rs`, `field_arc.rs`, `field_ray.rs`): one `SdfTool` / `RevKind` for the meridian, as the union of the convex atoms. The convex sweep of `field_sweep.rs` stays valid for each atom.
3. Bounds: the cut uses the OUTER bound of a concave arc for the gouge verdict (`deviate`). The rest material that a later operation reads (`crates/app/src/rest/ahead.rs`) uses the INNER bound, so no later operation assumes that material is gone when it is not.
4. `rest::ahead` and `stamp_tool` (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp_tool.rs`) hash the tip form, the tip diameter and the `FormMill` outline.
5. The display reads the same solid.
6. The existing variants for the old kinds stay. A test proves each one equal to its meridian solid before any later issue replaces it.

## Rules

- `effort:max`: the stock simulation (safety floor).
- The old kinds keep identical stock results and digests (pinned).

## Done means

- Column and field engines agree within `DEV_TOL` on straight and arc cuts with a flat-tip taper, a tapered ball nose, a roundover bit and a cove bit (pinned).
- The inner and outer bounds differ by no more than the sag limit (pinned).
- A change of tip form or outline changes the stamp and the rest digest (pinned).

title: STEP import removes a short edge from a Fusion solid and then refuses the enlarged gap

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happens

CamCraft refuses a Fusion STEP model of a heater block. The user reproduced the failure in the desktop app on macOS (v0.24.0, commit `e6e04f5d0`). The MCP tool `import_model` gives the same result. Two AP214 exports and one AP242 export contain the same edge geometry. All three give this diagnostic:

```text
import_model: corrupt STEP: solidcore: import_step produced an invalid result: 1 of 1 solid item(s) refused; first #14 at check: a vertex sits 1.157e-2 mm off its edges (limit 1e-3) - re-export the model, or import an STL
```

The user can view an STL copy. A STEP copy exported from FreeCAD gives the same gap. The original CAD files stay local.

### Where the gap comes from

A diagnostic probe built the same STEP record twice with the pinned Solidcore version (`2016386`). Only the healing setting changed.

| Measurement | Before healing | After normal import healing |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Edges in the solid | 999 | 998 |
| Gap at the start of spline edge `#3375` | 0.006223 mm | 0.011573 mm |
| Largest vertex-to-endpoint gap in the solid | 0.007736 mm | 0.011573 mm |

The file defines edge `#3407` between vertices `#2564` and `#2120`. The vertices are 0.009944 mm apart. Spline edge `#3375` starts at `#2564`. Healing removes `#3407` and redirects `#3375` to `#2120`. Measuring from that vertex to the same spline endpoint reproduces the reported gap. The diagnostic names the solid (`#14`), so the user cannot identify the affected edge.

FreeCAD (Open CASCADE) keeps both vertices and all 999 edges. It reports one valid, closed solid with 345 faces. The file declares 0.010 mm uncertainty.

### Two limits still apply

The largest gap before healing already exceeds CamCraft's fixed 0.001 mm vertex limit. A separate probe passed the reader's record to the machining mesher at the normal 0.005 mm chord target. The mesher refused face 0 with a measured deviation of 0.011141 mm. Increasing the vertex limit alone would still leave a mesh refusal.

### Decision requested

Can the importer preserve an explicit short edge when collapsing it increases the endpoint error on an adjacent edge? If the preserved solid still exceeds machining tolerance, should CamCraft offer a reduced-fidelity view or refuse it with the measured accuracy? Issue #2976 and PR #2994 provide a precedent for reduced fidelity on an edge-to-surface gap. This case concerns a vertex and a curve endpoint.

**Done means:** A synthetic STEP regression fixture covers two distinct vertices joined by a short edge beside a spline. The test checks the edge count and the endpoint error before and after healing. A second test pins the agreed import outcome when the source exceeds machining tolerance. The user can see which check failed and the measured gap. Machining checks continue to use the accuracy the importer achieved.

**Triage.** P3 because direct STEP import fails and an STL copy works for viewing. `effort:high` because the fix changes geometry repair and needs a regression test.

[STEP build and validation](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs#L297-L337) · [Vertex limit and measurement](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_import.rs#L106-L157)

title: 2D Chamfer: select a tip offset

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Wanted

A 2D Chamfer can state a tip offset. The cone then cuts the requested chamfer through a radial band above that radius.

This lets the user keep the selected edge and the requested chamfer width. For example, a 6 mm chamfer mill can cut a 1 mm chamfer at a 2 mm tip offset. The cutting band is then 2 mm to 3 mm from the tool axis.

## Current behaviour

CamCraft places the virtual cone tip on the selected wall. It keeps the tip at:

```text
tip_z = top_z - width * tan(angle)
```

The tool centre has no XY offset from the picked line. A larger chamfer mill therefore cuts through the smallest part of its cone. The operation has no setting that moves to a larger-radius band of the same cone.

## Proposed rule

For an ideal sharp cone, add one operation value named `Tip offset`.

```text
tip offset = r
chamfer width = w
centreline offset toward air = r
tip_z = top_z - (r + w) * tan(chamfer angle)
contact radius = r to r + w
```

For a 45-degree chamfer, a 6 mm tool, `w = 1 mm`, and `r = 2 mm`:

```text
centreline offset = 2 mm
contact radius = 2 mm to 3 mm
tip_z = top_z - 3 mm
```

The final chamfer stays 1 mm wide. The tool uses a 2 mm to 3 mm part of the cone instead of its 0 mm to 1 mm part.

The `Side` setting determines the air side for closed rings and selected open chains.

## Safety doors

- Refuse when `r` is negative or not finite.
- Refuse when the tool radius is smaller than `r + width`.
- Refuse when the cone or flute reach cannot supply `(r + width) * tan(angle)`.
- Offset closed loops and open chains with the same air-side law.
- Refuse an offset that folds, disappears, or reaches material on the air side.
- Keep the declared `EdgeBreak` on the original picked edge with the authored width and depth. The larger contact band must not create credit for more edge work.
- Stock simulation and collision verification must judge the offset cone position, not the old tip-on-wall position.

## Scope

This issue does not model or compensate for tool-tip wear. It selects a band of the current ideal sharp cone.

Issue #895 is related because it tracks real flat, ball, and radiused tip geometry. This operation-level feature can be specified independently.

## Done means

- The Geometry page exposes `Tip offset` for a 2D Chamfer.
- The value round-trips through project files and the MCP operation parameter surface.
- A 45-degree, 6 mm ideal cone cuts an authored 1 mm chamfer with a 2 mm tip offset.
- A test proves the contact radii are 2 mm and 3 mm, and the tip path is 3 mm below the top plane.
- A motion test proves a closed ring offsets toward the side `Side` names.
- A motion test proves each selected open chain offsets toward its air side.
- The tool-radius and flute-reach refusals name the missing dimension.
- Stock simulation proves the final 1 mm edge break and no gouge on the part.
- Existing 0 mm tip offset projects keep the current path byte for byte.

## Labels

Suggested triage: `enhancement`, `area:2d`, `P6`, and `effort:high`.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer can use a selected larger-radius band of a chamfer mill while preserving the authored chamfer width.

title: Research: conversational (no-model) G-code operations - what shops expect, what we lack

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Research only - no code from this issue. Pick never takes it for code (AGENTS.md "needs-research").

**Why.** Conversational systems (shop-floor forms on the control or a PC: e.g. Kentech's KipwareM/T, Mazatrol, PathPilot conversational, Heidenhain Klartext cycles, LinuxCNC NGCGUI) generate G-code from a few numbers with no CAD model: bolt-hole circles, frames and pockets, keyways, grooves, threads, facing to size. Users who never open CAD (e.g. a WorkBee owner on Discord: making a 3D part from a 2D sketch is "too much of a hassle") would use CamCraft for these if it offered them. Asked by the user (mkinney) 2026-11-20.

**Clean-room boundary.** Other vendors' public feature lists are used only as a checklist of *which* operations shops expect. Never copied: their wording, UI labels, parameter names, screen layouts or dialog flows. Each operation's behaviour is specced from machining handbooks and public G-code standards, as for any operation. Whether AGENTS.md's reference list should name "public feature lists of other products, for gap finding only" is a question for the maintainer.

**Open questions**
1. Which conversational operations are common across systems (mill and lathe)? A table: operation, which systems have it, what inputs it needs in machining terms.
2. Which of those CamCraft already covers (existing operations that would work from a sketch or stock alone), which need only a new "from numbers" front end, and which are genuinely new toolpath work?
3. Where does it live: a "quick op" that makes its own sketch geometry and a normal operation (undoable commands + MCP tools), versus a separate wizard? Recommendation needed.
4. Output style: canned cycles and cutter comp where the post supports them (conversational users expect short, readable programs) versus expanded moves.
5. Priority order for sub-issues, by how many users it helps.

**Done means:** the questions answered in comments here, the sub-issues filed (each with one P*, one effort:*, area:*, source:agent, a "Done means" line and "Part of #this"), linked back, `needs-research` dropped and this umbrella closed.

Related: #2227 (Heidenhain Klartext dialect), #1880 (SVG import).

1. **3D Pocket, strategy adaptive**, Ø12 flat, stepdown 2, stepover 2, leave 0.3: **334 s**. Six levels hit the planning budget, eight more self-cross, and all of those fall back to Offset rings - but the op reports status ok and **warnings=0**; the fallback is only in the notes:
   `adaptive: the HSM plan is refused: growing the cleared area ran past its planning budget after 57 revolutions ... ~607.9 k outline vertices processed (limit 600 k) ... - Offset rings cut the level at Z 28.000 instead`
2. **Rest 3D Pocket** with a Ø6 ball (rest_rough): **765 s**, same fallbacks.
3. **finish3d pattern waterline**, Ø6 ball, tolerance 0.05: no answer after **900 s** (MCP client timeout). A `save_project` and a read-only `get_job` queued behind it also time out at 900 s each: the server serves nothing while one generate runs, and there is no cancel tool. The run ended without a saved Rest6 result or a post.

## Expected
Toolpaths for a part this size in well under a minute (or a refusal naming the budget); a fallback that replaces most of the requested strategy is a warning, not a note; a long generate does not block save/read calls, or can be cancelled.

## Reproduce (on len)
`/home/mikekinney/qa/runs/20261120-q02-3d-mold/q02-3d-mold.camproj` (STL model) -> `open_project`, `generate {name:"Rough12"}`, `generate {name:"Rest6"}`, `generate {name:"Waterline6"}`. Op parameters: `/home/mikekinney/qa/runs/20261120-q02-3d-mold/evidence-57.json`; results `evidence-55.json`, `-69`, `-70`, `-76`, `-83`, `-85`; report `/home/mikekinney/qa/runs/20261120-q02-3d-mold/REPORT.md` (problems 3 and 5).

Related: #5, #882, #1950.

Not checked on current main.

Done means: Rough12, Rest6 and Waterline6 on this part each finish within a stated budget (or refuse with a reason), the adaptive fallback raises a warning, and a long generate no longer blocks other MCP calls (or can be cancelled); pinned by tests.

body:
## Goal

Add vertical-plane mirror support to pattern folders so users can program one half of a symmetrical part and mirror its toolpaths to the other half with full model verification. Depends on the CL toolpath transforms, pattern folder, and pattern verification sub-issues of `#2938`.

## Scope

- **Mirror mode (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`, commands, MCP, project file):** Add `Mirror { plane_point, plane_normal, cut_direction, keep_original }` to `PatternDef`.
  - Allow vertical planes only (`nz == 0`); refuse horizontal or tilted mirror planes at command creation.
  - Add `MirrorCutDirection` with `PreserveClimb` (default) and `GeometricMirror`.
  - Support `keep_original` (default `true`, matching copies `0` and `1`; copy `0` can also be disabled via `disabled_instances`).
- **Transform and posting (`crates/cl/src/cl/transform.rs`, `crates/app/src/posting.rs`):**
  - Under `GeometricMirror`, reflect moves, flip `arc.ccw` (`G2` <-> `G3`), and swap `CompSide` (`G41` <-> `G42`).
  - Under `PreserveClimb`, use safe per-pass reversal for 2D contours, profiles, and chamfers, and refuse by name any operation with ramps, adaptive clearing, or multi-pass roughing that cannot reverse safely.
  - Refuse unsupported operation kinds (turning, threading, probing, wire EDM, sinker EDM, tilted 5-axis moves) by name.
- **Full model verification (`crates/app/src/posting.rs`, `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs`):**
  - Carve the mirrored copy into the stock simulation and judge it against the full part mesh (`deviate`).
  - Run live model gouge, shank, and rapid-in-stock verification (`crates/sim/src/verify/`, `crates/app/src/operation/kept_rejudge.rs`) and fixture checks on every mirrored toolpath so sub-lattice gouges and shank hits on the mirrored side block the post.

## Done means

Tests mirror a symmetrical pocket and contour part across an X or Y vertical plane, verify `PreserveClimb` keeps climb direction on 2D contours and refuses unsafe multi-pass reversal by name, verify `GeometricMirror` flips `G2`/`G3` and `G41`/`G42` in golden NC output, and prove that a gouge on the mirrored side blocks the post.

body:
## Goal

Add a pattern folder entity inside a setup for linear and grid patterns, with undoable commands, MCP tools, project persistence, and expanded-move G-code posting. This is the smallest end-to-end slice of `#2938` (depends on the CL toolpath transforms sub-issue of `#2938`).

## Scope

- **Schema (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`):** Add a `PatternDef` component with `setup: Option<String>`, `suppressed: bool`, `order_mode` (`ByTool` default, `ByPart`), `kind` (`Linear { dir, count, spacing }`, `Grid { dir1, count1, spacing1, dir2, count2, spacing2 }`), `members: Vec<String>`, and `disabled_instances: Vec<u32>`. Use `OperationMeta::order` to position the folder in the setup list (same pattern as `ProgramEntry` in `crates/app/src/program_entry.rs`).
- **Rules:** All copies use the WCS of the parent setup (`crates/app/src/setup.rs`). An operation belongs to at most one folder in the same setup. Refuse nested folders. Validate finite positive counts and spacing at command creation.
- **Commands (`crates/app/src/commands/`):** Add undoable `CreatePatternFolder`, `EditPatternFolder`, `SetPatternMembers`, `SetPatternInstanceEnabled`, and `DeletePatternFolder` (ungroups member operations by default). Extend `ReorderOperation` and `RenameOperation` to support pattern folders.
- **MCP (`crates/app/src/mcp/`):** Add `create_pattern_folder`, `edit_pattern_folder`, `set_pattern_members`, `set_pattern_instance_enabled`, and `delete_pattern_folder`, and report pattern folders in `get_job`.
- **Project file (`crates/app/src/project/`):** Persist pattern folders as a new entity kind so older builds refuse the file cleanly instead of dropping folders silently.
- **Expanded posting (`crates/app/src/posting.rs`):**
  - Expand enabled copies using `cl::transform::translate`.
  - In `ByTool` mode, run each member operation in folder order across all enabled copies inside one `SECTION` with safe clearance-plane rapid links between copies so shipped posts (`assets/posts/*.cps`) do not emit redundant `T.. M6` tool changes.
  - In `ByPart` mode, run all member operations at one enabled copy before moving to the next enabled copy.
  - Preserve `viewer_map` line-to-position mapping for every expanded copy.

## Done means

Tests create, edit, reorder, undo, redo, save, and reload a linear pattern folder and a grid pattern folder through commands and MCP, disable one copy, and pin deterministic golden NC output for `ByTool` (without redundant tool changes between copies) and `ByPart` orders.

PR B of #917 (branch `issue/917-solidcore-step`) meshes STEP files through solidcore. The new mesh of `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` and `testdata/models/fig8.step` is finer. Three toolpath tests now fail. They pass on the head of #2843 (`eae027d55`). The PR marks them `known-fail #2849`. Their asserts do not change.

1. `lead_approach::the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent` (line 247). The stock-source pocket with `Entry3D::Helix` gives these notes:
   - `entry: the horizontal arc entry does not fit (...) - the entry descends onto the pass start without it`
   - `entry: the pass start (-31.878, 8.513) at Z 17.500 is in material and the helix fits only away from the pass start - ramp along the pass instead` (and the same at Z 15, 12.5, 10)
   - `2D Pocket: the check for corners of the stock tighter than the tool did not run (invalid geometry: loop crosses itself) - look at the stock corners around the part`
2. `lead_approach::an_axis_aligned_lead_start_posts_the_users_arc_entry_as_g18_or_g19` (line 131). The contour with `axis_start` gets no vertical arc. Notes:
   - `entry: oblique vertical arc posted as chords - no standard plane`
   - `depth: the ring at (-0.333, -7.491) ends at its floor Z 0.000 - the part is solid below it; levels below skipped (-5.000, -7.000)`
3. `shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` (line 312). The last feed ends 31.406 mm from the part outline. The test expects 4 mm (the tool radius). The path verifies clean and posts.

## Safety

No result is silent wrong output. Tests 1 and 2 state each fallback in a note. Test 3 verifies clean. But the corner check in `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs` does not run, and the user sees only the note.

## The defect

The "loop crosses itself" error comes from `Region::normalize` in `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs` (line 233). A region that the corner check builds from the new mesh outline has a self-crossing loop. Find which loop it is, and why the solidcore mesh makes it. Then check if tests 1 to 3 have the same cause.

## Done when

- The three tests pass with no change to their asserts.
- The `known-fail #2849` markers are removed.

labels.name: enhancement

body:
What happens:
CamCraft has Rotary Contour (waterline rings), Rotary Parallel (generatrix passes along axis), and Rotary Offset (radial roughing) for turned parts. It also has Flow5D (auto-computed direction field, 5-axis tilt) and MultiAxisContour (picked edge chains, 5-axis tilt). There is no operation that combines:
- A rotary axis (A/B/C) as primary continuous motion
- Picked edge chains defining helical flow lines
- Radial tool pose (tool axis points to rotation axis)
- Laid-down planning frame (like Rotary Parallel)

Expected:
A new "Rotary Flow" operation (also called Cylindrical Flow) that:
1. Fits the axis of revolution from the model (shared with rotary twins)
2. Lays the part down in a planning frame (local X = axis, local Z ≈ world up)
3. Accepts picked edge chains that define helical flow lines on the surface
4. Generates passes along local X that follow the picked chains in the laid frame
5. Steps between chains in local Y (which maps to rotary angle)
6. Poses the tool radially on every cut move (shared radial pose law)
7. Stamps C-axis angles when the machine has a spindle C (shared with Rotary Contour)

Evidence:
Requested for machining injection screws, augers, propeller blades, turbine blades - any helical surface where the user defines flow lines by picking edges.

Done means:
- New operation kind "Rotary Flow" in MultiAxis section
- Requires ball-nose tool
- Accepts edge chain picks as geometry source
- Parameters: stepover (distance between flow lines), tolerance, clearance/retract/top/bottom Z, feed, plunge_feed, climb, lead/lag/max_tilt_deg
- Works on mill-turn (C-axis) and 4-axis mill (A/B-axis)
- Posts C-axis angles when machine has spindle C
- Verified by stock simulation and fixture checks

body:
## What the user sees

The import of a user STEP file with a twisted B-spline flank stops with this refusal:

`a boundary point lies off the surface, outside its knot domain`

The file is legal. A different tool that reads STEP through solidcore opens the same file. The file is private and is not attached.

## Where

- The refusal comes from `Fault::Outside` in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_nearest.rs:112`.
- The import path is the truck-stepio path.

## Cause, as found

- The surface is a degree-3 B-spline surface with a strong twist.
- The Newton search for the nearest surface point lands on a neighbouring sheet of the surface.
- The rescue grid has 4 samples for each knot span. On this surface the grid is too coarse to find the correct sheet.
- The defect is of the same class as #1602.

## Possible fixes

- Import STEP through solidcore (#917). This is the full fix.
- Or make the rescue search denser, or make it use the trim boundary.

The work decides between these and records the decision.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with a strongly twisted degree-3 B-spline face, imports without the refusal. The fixture is not the user's file.
- A boundary point that is off the surface by more than the tolerance still gives the refusal.
- The import does not become slower by a large factor on the current fixtures.

## Effort

The importer makes geometry. Thus the safety floor applies and the effort is `effort:high`.

title: Research: XYUV wire EDM - heal swallowtails when the kerf radius exceeds a local radius (instead of refusing)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

body:
**Research only.** No code until the open questions below are answered and the concrete sub-issues are filed (AGENTS.md "needs-research is research, not code").

## Where this comes from

A wire EDM user, Alex (@alextreseder; CamCraft Discord, 2026-11-19), asked whether our XYUV (+Z) path is collision-aware and handles swallowtails. His points, in short:

- The easy case: the wire (kerf) radius is smaller than every local radius of the part. Then each ruled face is offset with an arc join and projected onto the XY and UV planes.
- The hard case: the radius is not smaller than all local radii. Then the degenerate **local and global swallowtails** must be healed and sewn with a bounded-tolerance technique. In general this is one of the hardest CAD-kernel problems, but for wire EDM it splits into **two 2D problems** (the XY and UV planes), which makes it tractable.
- He has a working procedure (currently a FreeCAD macro) and offered to share it.

## What CamCraft does today (main)

- 4-axis ruled wire cut (#537): an upper and a lower closed profile, paired into rulings by normalised arc length or by sync points (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled.rs`, `pairing.rs`); per-ruling widening (#1170, `ruled_widen.rs`).
- Kerf: each profile is offset in 2D, and the rulings are laid over those parallels.
- Degenerate results are **refused, not healed**: the fold law (the ruled surface folds back between rulings) and the crossing law (the surface crosses itself at the quarter heights) in `ruled_laws.rs`, plus the kerf and gouge laws, run before the path leaves the generator.

So the easy case works, and the hard case gives a refusal with a reason. Healing is the gap.

## Open questions

1. Which swallowtail cases occur in practice for XYUV: local (one corner tighter than the kerf radius) and global (two distant parts of a profile approach each other), on the XY plane, the UV plane, or both, and when the two planes disagree?
2. What is the healing procedure? Trim the self-intersections of each 2D offset (published offset-curve methods), then re-pair the rulings? How is the pairing kept consistent when one plane loses a loop the other plane keeps?
3. What tolerance bounds the healing, and how is the result checked (the fold and crossing laws must still pass on the healed surface)?
4. When healing changes the cut part (a corner the wire cannot reach), how is that shown to the user: the existing uncut-corner note, or a refusal when the change is above a tolerance?
5. Which of today's refusals would become healed results, and which must stay refusals (Prime Directive: correct or visibly refused)?

## What would help (from Alex or anyone)

- A **written description** of the procedure: steps, tolerances, how local vs. global swallowtails are sewn.
- If the macro itself is shared: its **licence**. We can reuse code only under a licence compatible with this project (MIT or Apache-2.0); otherwise we implement from the description and from published literature.
- **Test shapes** that make local and global swallowtails (simple STEP or DXF profiles, upper and lower). These become test fixtures for the fold and crossing laws even before any healing exists.

Clean-room: published literature, the contributor's own description, and our own design notes only; no material from Autodesk products.

## Done means

The questions above are answered in comments, and the concrete sub-issues are filed (each with one P*, one effort label, area labels, a Done-means line and "Part of #this"); then this umbrella is closed.

body:
Part of #2525 (slice 4 of 6). The maintainer set the priority on 2026-11-18: "GPU shader issues get priority".

Depends on #2613 (the evaluator seam and the CPU reference). Start only when #2614 records "go".

## What to add

A GPU implementation of the evaluator seam of #2613, native only (DX12, Vulkan, Metal):

- New files in `camcraft-ui`, for example `crates/ui/src/nest_gpu.rs` and `crates/ui/src/nest_raster.wgsl`. Follow the pattern of `crates/ui/src/trace.rs`: `egui_wgpu::wgpu`, error scopes, a device-lost watch, no `unwrap`.
- The CPU rasterises (#2612). The GPU receives only bit-packed `u32` rows of the sheet and the part.
- **Integer kernel only:** AND, `countOneBits`, integer adds. No float enters the decision.
- **Order-free result:** the first legal position is an `atomicMin` of the packed key of #2613 (row, column, rotation index). Or the kernel returns the full count map and the CPU scans it.
- Check `DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS` and the device limits (`max_storage_buffer_binding_size`, `max_compute_workgroups_per_dimension`) before the build. Use tiles that fit the limits.
- **Refuse, then fall back.** No adapter, no compute, a small limit, a validation error or a lost device gives an `Err` with a reason. The caller then uses the CPU evaluator. The log names the reason. The nest result does not change.
- The exact vector check stays on the CPU (#2613).

## Laws

- The CPU path is the reference. The GPU path gives the same answer, bit for bit.
- The same input gives the same layout on each machine, with or without a GPU.

## Notes

- No new crate edge: `camcraft-ui` already depends on `camcraft-app`, which re-exports `camcraft-geometry`. No new third-party dependency: `wgpu` 30.0.1 is in the lock through `egui-wgpu`. If the work needs a direct `wgpu` dependency or a new crate, stop: that needs a decision entry and the owner's decision at review.
- Record the kernel layout, the tile size and the fallback rules in `docs/decisions/<issue>-<slug>.md`.

body:
Part of #2574 (research answer 2).

The maintainer named the Solidcraft route in #2574: "Or use solidcrafts model with the joints defined in the solidcraft file. Either way i guess. if we go the solidcraft route a base model could be generated thru its MCP."

## Recommended in #2574
The contract is a file, not a live MCP call. Solidcraft (MIT OR Apache-2.0) exports an assembly with its joints as URDF (`export` tool, `docs/mcp.md` of tangency-labs/solidcraft). URDF is a public XML format (wiki.ros.org/urdf/XML): links, `revolute` and `prismatic` joints, `origin`, `axis`, `limit`, mesh references. `camcraft-sim` reads only the file and never needs Solidcraft at run time. Without a URDF, the model comes from the `.mch` (#2584, #2591).

## Open design points
1. The `.mch` key that names the URDF and maps each URDF joint to an axis letter.
2. The units and the root frame of the URDF against the machine frame and the `travel` of the `.mch`. Which file wins when the joint limits differ.
3. The mesh formats to read (STL and OBJ readers exist; GLB does not).
4. Refusals: a joint with no letter, a letter with no joint, a closed chain, a mesh that is not found.

## Done means
The design points have answers in comments, and the code sub-issue is filed with a `P*`, `effort:*` and `area:*` label. No hard dependency on Solidcraft is added.

title: Research: turning on a mill (part in the spindle, lathe tools on the table, one WCS per tool), e.g. Tormach RapidTurn on a 770MX

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Asked by mkinney (2026-11-18), who has a Tormach 770MX: "you can use a 3d mill like a lathe ... You end up using multiple WCS for each tool and put part in spindle". Wording: this is **turning on a mill (part in spindle)**, not live tooling on a lathe (CamCraft's existing "Mill-turn" machine).

## The setup

- The workpiece is held in a collet in the mill spindle and turns (M3/M4 at lathe speeds).
- Lathe tools (turning, facing, grooving, threading, parting) are clamped on the table in a gang row.
- There is no tool change: each tool is selected by switching to its own work offset (G54...G59, G59.1-3, G54.1 Pn) whose origin is that tool's tip relative to the spindle centre line.
- One length offset describes the part in the spindle: collet nose to the end of the stock stick-out (`G43 H<n>` once; the user keeps T255 for it).
- Lathe Z (along the part) is the mill Z; lathe X (diameter) is a table axis toward the spindle centre line.

## What CamCraft does today (QA run p09, main `83867fd7`)

- No way to declare "part in spindle, tools on the table".
- A lathe operation set accepted on a 3-axis mill machine posts lathe code labelled "Tormach 770MX" with no warning (high; filed separately).

## Open questions

1. Machine description: a part-in-spindle mode, tool stations on the table (position, side of the spindle, WCS), the collet nose and the stock stick-out.
2. Operations: reuse the turning operations; what changes in the X sign and spindle direction per side; constant surface speed vs fixed RPM on a mill spindle; feed per rev.
3. Post: a WCS switch per tool, no M6, safe retracts between stations, the one `G43 H` for the stock.
4. Safety checks: tool blocks vs the collet and the part, max spindle RPM with a part in it, chip direction.
5. Sources: Tormach's public RapidTurn documentation (operator manual UM10393, D32901, TD10561); the user's own 770MX tests.

Plan (user): several CamCraft simulations first, then PathPilot Hub, then air cuts, then real cuts - slowly.

title: SolidCraft .sc import refuses designs with fillets or blends: native B-rep 'unknown variant blend'

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found by the QA runs of 2026-11-18 (SolidCraft v0.44.1 designs -> CamCraft main `83867fd7`), parts p06 (all-ops mill part) and p07 (lathe shaft); both have fillets or blend faces.

What happens: `import_model <design>.sc` refuses the design:
`Solidcraft design refused: import_solidcraft: invalid input: the final body does not decode: native B-rep: unknown variant 'blend', expected one of 'plane', ..., 'placed_revolution'`.

SolidCraft 0.44 writes a `blend` surface kind that CamCraft's `.sc` reader (#1456) does not know. Designs without fillets import. Every design with a fillet, round or blend - most real parts - is refused, so the "open SolidCraft files directly" path does not work for them.

Workarounds today: export STEP from SolidCraft (but see the STEP mesh-gap issue the same runs found) or STL.

Done means: a `.sc` design with fillets from the current SolidCraft release imports with the same body as its STEP export (a pinned fixture `.sc` with a blend face, and a test). Track the next SolidCraft surface kinds the same way (the QA runs re-check each SolidCraft release).

title: Research: component-based tool assemblies (inserts, holders, adapters with mounting frames, linked to the library)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
**Need (from a user, in our words):** Users keep one insert and many holders that accept it. Today each CamCraft tool is a separate whole, so the same insert is defined again in every holder. Wanted: a component library (inserts, holders, adapters, extensions), each with its own mounting coordinate system; holders state which inserts they accept; an assembly is built from components and stays linked, so a change to a component updates every assembly that uses it. Parametric tools remain and can serve as components.

**Reference:** ISO 13399 (cutting tool data representation: tool items, adaptive items, coordinate systems and connection interfaces). Clean-room: no competitor material.

**Related:** #1039 (lathe holder bodies placed by ISO 13399 coordinate systems), #1040 (tool bodies assembled from several vendor models), #2092 (a tool's library holder becomes a reference - the first step toward linked components).

**Open questions:**
1. Data model: which component kinds (insert, holder, adapter, extension, collet/chuck); which ISO 13399 coordinate systems and connection codes do we need?
2. Compatibility: how does a holder declare the inserts it takes (ISO insert shape, size, seat), and how do we refuse a wrong combination by name?
3. Linking: library references vs copies in a project; what happens when a linked component changes; project-file format and migration (relates to #2092).
4. Geometry: how the assembly's cutting edge, gauge line and body (for collision checks) are derived from the components' frames (relates to #1039, #1040).
5. Milling too? Indexable face mills and end mills use the same idea (body plus inserts).
6. UI and MCP: how users browse "holders that take this insert", and the commands needed (Everything Is a Command).

**Done means:** each question answered in a comment, a recorded design decision, and concrete sub-issues filed (each with P/effort/area), then this umbrella is closed.

body:
Extract 2D nesting outlines from 3D models (`STEP`, `STL`, `OBJ`, and `.sc` `#1456`) and instance 2.5D/3D operations at each placed part on a router sheet.

Depends on #2158, #2160, and #2161.

## Scope

- **3D orientation and sheet-face selection (`crates/app/`, `crates/geometry/`):**
  - Allow a user to pick a planar face (`FeatureSel::Face` or `FeatureSel::Patch`) on a 3D model to lie flat on the sheet (`normal -> -Z`), or default to the model's current `-Z` base face (`z_min` seated at `z = 0`).
  - Store the chosen sheet-face orientation on the `NestPart` entry (undoable command parameter).
- **2D silhouette extraction and thickness checks (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/slice.rs`):**
  - Project the oriented 3D mesh along the sheet normal via `slice::project` (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/slice.rs`) to obtain the outer loop and through-holes (`Region`).
  - Measure model height `z_max - z_min`. Refuse by model name when `model_height > sheet_thickness` within tolerance.
- **Flat-extrusion check vs 2.5D/3D router instancing:**
  - Compare `slice::at_z` cross-sections at bottom, mid, and top planes against `slice::project` to detect non-flat features (pockets, blind holes, steps, chamfers).
  - On pure 2D through-cut nests (`Kind::Waterjet`, `Kind::Plasma`), refuse non-flat 3D parts by name unless the user explicitly enables `outline_only`.
  - On `Kind::Mill` (CNC router) nests, nest using the full outer XY silhouette plus cutter diameter and gap, then replicate the part's authored 2.5D/3D operations (`Pocket`, `Drill`, `Chamfer2D`, `Contour`, `Pocket3D`) transformed to each placed instance `(tx, ty, angle_deg)` on the sheet setup.
  - Sequence all internal 2.5D/3D operations across all placed instances before outer `Contour` cutout passes so hold-down stays intact.

## Done means

Tests load a 3D `STEP`/`STL` bracket and a pocketed 2.5D plate, orient a chosen face onto the sheet, refuse parts taller than the sheet thickness by name, refuse non-flat parts on waterjet/plasma unless `outline_only` is set, and nest plus generate transformed 2.5D router toolpaths on every placed instance with outer cutouts running last.

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-15, with the DXF work of #1452.

His words: "A DXF should be possible to "place" on a stock and used as references for cutting - not be treated like a model - thus for processes like wireedm, plasma, laser, etc etc.. we can just make a sheet, cube, cylinder. place the DXF - and select operations accordingly."

What is missing: the sub-issues of #1452 give DXF sketches to the milling operations (#1864, #1867, #1868, #1869) and to the plasma profile (#1870). No issue gives them to Wire EDM or to a laser cut.

Scope:

1. Wire EDM 2-axis profile on DXF sketch chains: the user picks closed or open chains, and the side and the direction for each chain. The kerf (wire radius and spark gap) offset uses the same law as the model-based Wire EDM operation.
2. The stock gives the top and the bottom of the cut. No solid model is necessary.
3. Laser: find out if a laser cut operation exists. If it exists, give it the same chain picking. If it does not exist, say so in a comment and file the issue for it. Do not add a laser operation in this issue.
4. The kerf verify law runs against the sketch chains. An offset that cannot fit (a slot narrower than the kerf, a self-crossing offset) refuses by name. It never posts a path that cuts on the wrong side.
5. The commands have their MCP tools, or a follow-up issue `MCP: <command>`.

This changes posted G-code (new programs). It is under the safety floor.

Done means:

- A setup with a sheet stock and a placed DXF profile posts a Wire EDM 2-axis program for a closed chain and for an open chain.
- Golden CL and posted goldens pin the side, the direction and the kerf offset.

body:
Found while the cut gate of v0.21.0 was red (run 43739171721, step `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`).

What happens:
- A whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy and no area control clears the stock around the part out to the stock outline (#1774, PR #1780).
- On the 60 mm bore part in 70 x 70 stock, each level is then a wide ring with the part as its island.
- The HSM plan exceeds its budgets on that ring: about 600.4k outline vertices against the limit 600k (605.2k on Windows), and 124740 moves against the limit 120000.
- Offset rings cut four of the five levels. The notes name each level. The path verifies clean. There is no gouge.

Expected: the Adaptive strategy plans the stock ring within its budgets, or the budgets fit that region.

Workaround: set Tool containment to Inside on the operation. Then the pocket plans only the bore and Adaptive cuts each level.

Evidence: `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. The cut repaired the test with Tool containment Inside (commit `bf752be65` on `release/v0.21.0`), thus the default case has no test now.

Done means: the default whole-model Adaptive 3D Pocket on that fixture cuts each level with the Adaptive plan, with no budget note, and a test pins it.

Add a clean-room abrasive-waterjet corner slowdown and pierce-timing model from published waterjet engineering literature (Hashish, Zeng and Kim, Momber and Kovacevic, public OMAX notes).

Depends on #1883 (`WaterjetProfile`).

## Scope

- **Physics corner slowdown (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/`):**
  - Model stream lag scaling with thickness and traverse speed without copying any vendor table or third-party Fusion post.
  - Detect sharp corners (deflection angle) and tight curve segments on generated `WaterjetProfile` contours.
  - Compute a thickness-scaled deceleration and acceleration zone length (`3 mm` to `10 mm` range in published practice, clamped per segment).
